sentences.zh: 席書，字文同，遂寧人。

translations.literal: Xi Shu, styled Wentong, was a native of Suining.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shu, styled Wentong, was a native of Suining.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年進士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongzhi he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the third year of the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 授郯城知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Tancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Tancheng.

sentences.zh: 入為工部主事，移戶部，進員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered service as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Works, was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, and was promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Works, was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, and rose to vice director.

sentences.zh: 十六年，雲南晝晦地震，命侍郎樊瑩巡視，奏黜監司以下三百余人。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, when Yunnan suffered daytime darkness and an earthquake, Vice Minister Fan Ying was ordered to inspect the region and memorialized the dismissal of more than three hundred officials from provincial commissioners downward.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, after Yunnan was struck by daytime darkness and an earthquake, Vice Minister Fan Ying was dispatched to inspect the province and recommended the dismissal of more than three hundred officials from provincial commissioners on down.

sentences.zh: 書上疏言：「災異系朝廷，不系雲南。

translations.literal: Shu submitted a memorial saying: "Calamities and anomalies concern the court, not Yunnan alone.
translations.idiomatic: Shu submitted a memorial stating: "Calamities and portents reflect conditions at court, not conditions in Yunnan alone.

sentences.zh: 如人元氣內損，然後瘡瘍發四肢。

translations.literal: It is like when a person's vital energy is damaged within, and only then do sores break out on the limbs.
translations.idiomatic: It is as when a person's vital energy is damaged within, and only then do sores erupt on the limbs.

sentences.zh: 朝廷，元氣也。

translations.literal: The court is the vital energy.
translations.idiomatic: The court is the vital energy.

sentences.zh: 雲南，四肢也。

translations.literal: Yunnan is the limbs.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan is the limbs.

sentences.zh: 豈可舍致毒之源，專治四肢之末？

translations.literal: How can one abandon the source of the poison and treat only the extremities of the limbs?
translations.idiomatic: How can one ignore the source of the poison and treat only the extremities?

sentences.zh: 今內府供應數倍往年，冗食官數千，投充校尉數萬，齋醮寺觀無停日，織造頻煩，賞賚逾度；

translations.literal: Now the inner palace's provisions are several times those of former years; supernumerary officials number in the thousands; enrolled guards number in the tens of thousands; fasting rites and temple observances continue without cease; weaving commissions are frequent; and rewards and gifts exceed all bounds.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace's provisions now run several times what they once did; thousands hold supernumerary posts; tens of thousands have enrolled as guards; fasting rites and temple observances never cease; weaving commissions come one after another; and rewards and gifts exceed all measure.

sentences.zh: 皇親奪民田，宦官增遣不已；

translations.literal: Imperial kinsmen seize the people's fields, and eunuchs are dispatched in ever greater numbers without end.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial kinsmen seize commoners' fields, and eunuch missions are dispatched in ever greater numbers without end.

sentences.zh: 大獄據招詞不敢辯，刑官亦不敢伸；

translations.literal: In major cases, defendants dare not dispute confessions extracted under torture, and judicial officials dare not intervene.
translations.idiomatic: In major trials, defendants dare not challenge confessions extracted under torture, and judicial officials dare not speak up.

sentences.zh: 大臣賢者未起用，小臣言事謫者未復；

translations.literal: Worthy senior ministers have not been recalled to office, and junior officials who spoke out and were banished have not been restored.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy senior ministers have not been brought back into service, and junior officials banished for speaking out have not been restored.

sentences.zh: 文武官傳升，名器大濫。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials receive irregular promotions, and titles and offices are greatly debased.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials receive irregular promotions, and titles and offices are greatly debased.

sentences.zh: 災異之警，偶泄雲南，欲以遠方外吏當之，此何理也？

translations.literal: The warning of calamity and anomaly happened by chance to appear in Yunnan, yet you wish to hold distant frontier officials accountable—what logic is this?
translations.idiomatic: The warning of calamity happened by chance to appear in Yunnan, yet distant frontier officials are to be held accountable—what logic is this?

sentences.zh: 漢遣八使巡行天下，張綱獨曰：『豺狼當道，安問狐貍。』

translations.literal: When the Han dispatched eight commissioners to tour the realm, Zhang Gang alone said: "When wolves and jackals block the road, why bother asking about foxes?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Han dispatched eight commissioners to tour the realm, Zhang Gang alone said: "When wolves and jackals block the road, why bother asking about foxes?"

sentences.zh: 今樊瑩職巡察，不能劾戚畹、大臣，獨考黜雲南官吏，舍本而治末。

translations.literal: Now Fan Ying's duty is inspection, yet he cannot impeach imperial in-laws and great ministers and instead examines and dismisses only Yunnan officials, abandoning the root to treat the branch.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ying's duty is inspection, yet he cannot impeach imperial in-laws and great ministers and instead examines and dismisses only Yunnan officials, abandoning the root to treat the branch.

sentences.zh: 乞陛下以臣所言弊政，一切厘革。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to reform entirely the corrupt policies I have described.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to reform entirely the corrupt policies I have described.

sentences.zh: 他大害當祛，大政當舉者，悉令所司條奏而興革之。」

translations.literal: As for other great evils that should be removed and great policies that should be enacted, order the responsible offices to submit detailed memorials and carry out reform."
translations.idiomatic: As for other great evils that should be removed and great policies that should be enacted, let the responsible offices submit detailed memorials and carry out reform."

sentences.zh: 時不能用。

translations.literal: At the time his advice was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his advice was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 武宗時，歷河南僉事、貴州提學副使。

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Wuzong, he served successively as Henan intendant and Guizhou vice education intendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Wuzong, he served successively as Henan intendant and Guizhou vice education intendant.

sentences.zh: 時王守仁謫龍場驛丞，書擇州縣子弟，延守仁教之，士始知學。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Shouren had been banished to serve as post station director at Longchang; Shu selected sons of prefectural and county families and invited Shouren to teach them, and scholars there first came to know learning.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Shouren had been banished to serve as post station director at Longchang; Shu selected sons of local families and invited Shouren to teach them, and the region's scholars first came to know learning.

sentences.zh: 屢遷福建左布政使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to left provincial administration commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted until he became left provincial administration commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠反，急募兵二萬討之。

translations.literal: When Prince Ning Zhu Chenhao rebelled, he urgently raised twenty thousand troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ning Zhu Chenhao rebelled, he urgently raised twenty thousand troops to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 至則賊已平，乃返。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the rebels had already been pacified, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived, the rebels had already been pacified, and he returned.

sentences.zh: 尋以右副都御史巡撫湖廣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 中官李鎮、張旸假進貢及禦鹽名斂財十余萬，書疏發之。

translations.literal: The eunuchs Li Zhen and Zhang Yang, under the pretext of tribute missions and imperial salt, extorted more than one hundred thousand in funds; Shu exposed them in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs Li Zhen and Zhang Yang, under the pretext of tribute missions and imperial salt, extorted more than one hundred thousand in funds; Shu exposed them in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年改南京兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing he was transferred to right vice minister of the Nanjing Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiajing he was transferred to right vice minister of the Nanjing Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 江南北大饑，奉命振江北。

translations.literal: When famine struck both south and north of the Yangzi, he was ordered to provide relief north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck both south and north of the Yangzi, he was ordered to provide relief north of the river.

sentences.zh: 令州縣十里一廠，煮糜哺之，全活無算。

translations.literal: He ordered prefectures and counties to set up relief stations every ten li, cooking gruel to feed the hungry, and saved countless lives.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered prefectures and counties to set up relief stations every ten li, cooking gruel to feed the hungry, and saved countless lives.

sentences.zh: 初，書在湖廣，見中朝議「大禮」未定，揣帝向張璁、霍韜，獻議言：「昔宋英宗以濮王第十三子出為人後，今上以興獻王長子入承大統。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Shu was in Huguang, he saw that the court debate over the "Great Rites" remained unsettled. Sensing the emperor's inclination toward Zhang Cong and Huo Tao, he submitted a proposal saying: "Formerly Emperor Yingzong of Song, thirteenth son of the Prince of Pu, was given out in adoption; the present emperor, eldest son of the Prince of Xing, has entered to succeed to the great succession.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Shu was in Huguang, he saw that the court debate over the "Great Rites" remained unsettled. Sensing the emperor's inclination toward Zhang Cong and Huo Tao, he submitted a proposal saying: "Formerly Emperor Yingzong of Song, thirteenth son of the Prince of Pu, was given out in adoption; the present emperor, eldest son of the Prince of Xing, has entered to succeed to the great succession.

sentences.zh: 英宗入嗣在袞衣臨禦之時，今上入繼在宮車晏駕之後。

translations.literal: Yingzong entered the succession while already robed and presiding over the court; the present emperor entered the succession after the imperial carriage had halted.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong entered the succession while already robed and presiding over the court; the present emperor entered the succession after the imperial carriage had halted.

sentences.zh: 議者以陛下繼統武宗，仍為興獻帝之子，別立廟祀，張璁、霍韜之議未為非也。

translations.literal: Those debating hold that since Your Majesty succeeded to the throne from Emperor Wuzong yet remain the son of Emperor Xingxian, a separate temple should be established for worship—the proposal of Zhang Cong and Huo Tao is not wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Those debating hold that since Your Majesty succeeded to the throne from Emperor Wuzong yet remain the son of Emperor Xingxian, a separate temple should be established for worship—the proposal of Zhang Cong and Huo Tao is not wrong.

sentences.zh: 然尊無二帝。

translations.literal: Yet in honor there cannot be two emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in honor there cannot be two emperors.

sentences.zh: 陛下於武宗親則兄弟，分則君臣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty to Wuzong is by kinship a brother, but by rank subject and sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty to Wuzong is by kinship a brother, but by rank subject and sovereign.

sentences.zh: 既奉孝宗為宗廟主，可復有他稱乎？

translations.literal: Since you already take Emperor Xiaozong as the ancestral temple's chief, can there be another title?
translations.idiomatic: Since you already take Emperor Xiaozong as the ancestral temple's chief, can there be another title?

sentences.zh: 宜稱曰『皇考興獻王』，此萬世不刊之典。

translations.literal: You should be styled "Imperial Father, Prince of Xing"—this is an immutable standard for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: You should style him "Imperial Father, Prince of Xing"—this is an immutable standard for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 禮臣三四執奏，未為失也。

translations.literal: That the ritual officials repeatedly submitted their objections three or four times was not wrong.
translations.idiomatic: That the ritual officials repeatedly submitted their objections three or four times was not wrong.

sentences.zh: 然禮本人情，陛下尊為天子，慈聖設無尊稱，可乎？

translations.literal: Yet ritual rests on human feeling: Your Majesty is honored as Son of Heaven—can the Empress Dowager be without an honorific title?
translations.idiomatic: Yet ritual rests on human feeling: Your Majesty is honored as Son of Heaven—can the Empress Dowager be without an honorific title?

sentences.zh: 故尊所生曰帝後，上慰慈闈，此情之不能已也。

translations.literal: Therefore to honor one's biological parent with the title of empress dowager and thereby comfort the inner palace—this feeling cannot be restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore to honor one's biological parent with the title of empress dowager and thereby comfort the inner palace—this feeling cannot be restrained.

sentences.zh: 為今日議，宜定號曰『皇考興獻帝』。

translations.literal: For today's debate, the title should be fixed as "Imperial Father, Emperor Xingxian."
translations.idiomatic: For today's debate, the title should be fixed as "Imperial Father, Emperor Xingxian."

sentences.zh: 別立廟大內，歲時祀太廟畢，仍祭以天子之禮，似或一道也。

translations.literal: Establish a separate temple within the inner palace; after the seasonal sacrifices at the Grand Ancestral Temple are completed, still offer sacrifice with the rites of the Son of Heaven—this seems a possible path.
translations.idiomatic: Establish a separate temple within the inner palace; after the seasonal sacrifices at the Grand Ancestral Temple are completed, still offer sacrifice with the rites of the Son of Heaven—this seems a possible path.

sentences.zh: 蓋別以廟祀則大統正而昭穆不紊，隆以殊稱則至愛篤而本支不淪，尊尊親親，並行不悖。

translations.literal: For by separate temple worship the great succession is set right and the ancestral order is not confused; by elevated and distinct titles deepest love is affirmed and the root branch is not degraded—honoring the honored and cherishing the kin can proceed together without contradiction.
translations.idiomatic: By separate temple worship the great succession is set right and the ancestral order is not confused; by elevated and distinct titles deepest love is affirmed and the root branch is not degraded—honoring the honored and cherishing kin can proceed together without contradiction.

sentences.zh: 至慈聖宜稱皇母某後，不可以興獻加之。

translations.literal: As for the Empress Dowager, she should be styled Empress Dowager So-and-so; the Xingxian designation cannot be applied to her.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Empress Dowager, she should be styled Empress Dowager So-and-so; the Xingxian designation cannot be applied to her.

sentences.zh: 獻，謚也，豈宜加於今日？」

translations.literal: Xian is a posthumous title—how can it be applied today?"
translations.idiomatic: Xian is a posthumous title—how can it be applied today?"

sentences.zh: 議既具，會中朝競詆張璁為邪說，書懼不敢上，而密以示桂萼，萼然其議。

translations.literal: Once the proposal was complete, the court happened to be denouncing Zhang Cong's views as heterodox heresy; Shu feared to submit it and secretly showed it to Gui E, who approved the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Once the proposal was complete, the court happened to be denouncing Zhang Cong's views as heterodox heresy; Shu feared to submit it and secretly showed it to Gui E, who approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，萼具疏並上之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, E prepared a memorial and submitted both together.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, E prepared a memorial and submitted both together.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，趣召入對。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and urgently summoned him for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and urgently summoned him for an audience.

sentences.zh: 無何，詔改稱獻帝為本生皇考，遂寢召命。

translations.literal: Before long an edict changed the title of the Xian Emperor to "Biological Imperial Father," and the summons was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict changed the title of the Xian Emperor to "Biological Imperial Father," and the summons was suspended.

sentences.zh: 會禮部尚書汪俊以爭建廟去位，特旨用書代之。

translations.literal: When Minister of Rites Wang Jun left office over the dispute about building a temple, a special edict appointed Shu to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Rites Wang Jun left office over the dispute about building a temple, a special edict appointed Shu to replace him.

sentences.zh: 故事，禮部長貳率用翰林官。

translations.literal: By precedent, the chief and vice ministers of Rites were usually drawn from the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, the chief and vice ministers of Rites were usually drawn from the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 是時廷臣排異議益力，書進又不由廷推，因交章詆書，至訾其振荒無狀，多侵漁。

translations.literal: At this time court officials pressed their opposition with greater force; Shu's advancement had not come through regular court recommendation, and they submitted memorial after memorial denouncing him, even accusing him of misconduct in famine relief and much embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: At this time court officials pressed their opposition with greater force; Shu's advancement had not come through regular court recommendation, and they submitted memorial after memorial denouncing him, even accusing him of misconduct in famine relief and much embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 書亦屢辭新命，並錄上《大禮考議》，且乞遣官勘振荒狀。

translations.literal: Shu also repeatedly declined the new appointment, submitted along with it his Examination of the Great Rites Debate, and requested officials be dispatched to investigate the famine relief.
translations.idiomatic: Shu also repeatedly declined the new appointment, submitted along with it his Examination of the Great Rites Debate, and requested officials be dispatched to investigate the famine relief.

sentences.zh: 帝為遣司禮中官，戶、刑二部侍郎，錦衣指揮往勘，而趣書入朝益急。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched eunuchs of the Directorate of Ceremonial, vice ministers of Revenue and Justice, and a commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard to investigate, while urgently pressing Shu to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched eunuchs of the Directorate of Ceremonial, vice ministers of Revenue and Justice, and a commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard to investigate, while urgently pressing Shu to come to court.

sentences.zh: 比至德州，則廷臣已伏闕哭爭，盡系詔獄。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Dezhou, court officials had already prostrated themselves weeping at the palace gate in protest and were all imprisoned by imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Dezhou, court officials had already prostrated themselves weeping at the palace gate in protest and were all imprisoned by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 書馳疏言：「議禮之家，名為聚訟。

translations.literal: Shu sent an urgent memorial saying: "Those debating ritual are called litigious disputants.
translations.idiomatic: Shu sent an urgent memorial saying: "Those debating ritual are called litigious disputants.

sentences.zh: 兩議相持，必有一是。

translations.literal: When two positions contend, one must be right.
translations.idiomatic: When two positions contend, one must be right.

sentences.zh: 陛下擇其是者，而非者不必深較。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should choose the right one; those in the wrong need not be pressed too harshly.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should choose the right one; those in the wrong need not be pressed too harshly.

sentences.zh: 乞宥其愆失，俾獲自新。」

translations.literal: I beg you to pardon their faults and allow them to reform."
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to pardon their faults and allow them to reform."

sentences.zh: 不允。

translations.literal: This was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: This was not granted.

sentences.zh: 其年八月入朝，帝慰勞有加。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year he entered court, and the emperor comforted and rewarded him generously.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of that year he entered court, and the emperor comforted and rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 逾月乃會廷臣大議，上奏曰：

translations.literal: More than a month later he convened the court officials for a great debate and submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later he convened the court officials for a great debate and submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 夫得三代傳統之義，遠出漢、唐繼嗣之私者，莫若《祖訓》。

translations.literal: To grasp the meaning of the Three Dynasties' transmission of succession, far surpassing the private concerns of Han and Tang adoption, nothing surpasses the Ancestral Instructions.
translations.idiomatic: To grasp the meaning of the Three Dynasties' transmission of succession, far surpassing the private concerns of Han and Tang adoption, nothing surpasses the Ancestral Instructions.

sentences.zh: 《祖訓》曰「朝廷無皇子，必兄終弟及。」

translations.literal: The Ancestral Instructions say: "When the court has no imperial son, elder brother's death must be followed by younger brother's succession."
translations.idiomatic: The Ancestral Instructions say: "When the court has no imperial son, elder brother's death must be followed by younger brother's succession."

sentences.zh: 則嗣位者實繼統，非繼嗣也。

translations.literal: Thus the one who succeeds to the throne actually inherits the succession, not an adoption.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the one who succeeds to the throne actually inherits the succession, not an adoption.

sentences.zh: 伯自宜稱皇伯考，父自宜稱皇考，兄自宜稱皇兄。

translations.literal: An uncle should naturally be styled Imperial Uncle-Father, a father Imperial Father, and an elder brother Imperial Elder Brother.
translations.idiomatic: An uncle should naturally be styled Imperial Uncle-Father, a father Imperial Father, and an elder brother Imperial Elder Brother.

sentences.zh: 今陛下於獻帝、章聖已去本生之稱，復下臣等大議。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has already removed the "biological" designation for the Xian Emperor and Empress Zhangsheng, yet submits us ministers to another great debate.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has already removed the "biological" designation for the Xian Emperor and Empress Zhangsheng, yet submits us ministers to another great debate.

sentences.zh: 臣書、臣璁、臣萼、臣獻夫及文武諸臣皆議曰：世無二首，人無二本。

translations.literal: Your ministers Shu, Cong, E, Xianfu, and all civil and military officials debate thus: the world has no two heads; a person has no two roots.
translations.idiomatic: Your ministers Shu, Cong, E, Xianfu, and all civil and military officials debate thus: the world has no two heads; a person has no two roots.

sentences.zh: 孝宗皇帝，伯也，宜稱皇伯考。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong is an uncle and should be styled Imperial Uncle-Father.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong is an uncle and should be styled Imperial Uncle-Father.

sentences.zh: 昭聖皇太后，伯母也，宜稱皇伯母。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Zhaosheng is an aunt and should be styled Imperial Aunt.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Zhaosheng is an aunt and should be styled Imperial Aunt.

sentences.zh: 獻皇帝，父也，宜稱皇考。

translations.literal: Emperor Xian is a father and should be styled Imperial Father.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xian is a father and should be styled Imperial Father.

sentences.zh: 章聖皇太后，母也，宜稱聖母。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Zhangsheng is a mother and should be styled Holy Mother.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Zhangsheng is a mother and should be styled Holy Mother.

sentences.zh: 武宗仍稱皇兄，莊肅皇后宜稱皇嫂。

translations.literal: Wuzong should still be styled Imperial Elder Brother; Empress Zhuangsu should be styled Imperial Sister-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong should still be styled Imperial Elder Brother; Empress Zhuangsu should be styled Imperial Sister-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 尤願陛下仰遵孝宗仁聖之德，念昭聖擁翊之功，孝敬益隆，始終無間，大倫大統兩有歸矣。

translations.literal: We especially hope Your Majesty will look up to follow Emperor Xiaozong's benevolent and sage virtue, remember Empress Zhaosheng's merit in supporting the succession, and increase filial reverence without break from beginning to end—then both great human relations and the great succession will each have their place.
translations.idiomatic: We especially hope Your Majesty will look up to follow Emperor Xiaozong's benevolent and sage virtue, remember Empress Zhaosheng's merit in supporting the succession, and increase filial reverence without break from beginning to end—then both great human relations and the great succession will each have their place.

sentences.zh: 奉神主而別立禰室，於至親不廢，隆尊號而不入太廟，於正統無幹，尊親兩不悖矣。

translations.literal: To enshrine the spirit tablet yet establish a separate ancestral chamber does not abandon one's closest kin; to elevate the honorific title yet not enter the Grand Ancestral Temple does not interfere with the orthodox succession—honoring the honored and cherishing kin are both preserved.
translations.idiomatic: To enshrine the spirit tablet yet establish a separate ancestral chamber does not abandon one's closest kin; to elevate the honorific title yet not enter the Grand Ancestral Temple does not interfere with the orthodox succession—honoring the honored and cherishing kin are both preserved.

sentences.zh: 一遵《祖訓》，允合聖經。

translations.literal: Following entirely the Ancestral Instructions, this fully accords with the sage classics.
translations.idiomatic: Following entirely the Ancestral Instructions, this fully accords with the sage classics.

sentences.zh: 復三代數千年未明之典禮，洗漢、宋悖經違禮之陋習，非聖人其孰能之。

translations.literal: Restoring ritual norms unclear for thousands of years since the Three Dynasties and cleansing the vulgar customs of Han and Song that violated the classics and ritual—who but a sage could accomplish this?
translations.idiomatic: Restoring ritual norms unclear for thousands of years since the Three Dynasties and cleansing the vulgar customs of Han and Song that violated the classics and ritual—who but a sage could accomplish this?

sentences.zh: 議上，詔布告天下，尊稱遂定。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict was promulgated throughout the realm and the honorific titles were settled.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, an edict was promulgated throughout the realm and the honorific titles were settled.

sentences.zh: 帝既加隆所生，中外獻諛希恩者紛然遝至。

translations.literal: Once the emperor had elevated his biological parents, flatterers seeking favor from within and without came in swarms.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor had elevated his biological parents, flatterers seeking favor from within and without came in swarms.

sentences.zh: 錦衣百戶隨全、光祿錄事錢子勛既以罪褫，希旨請遷獻帝顯陵梓宮北葬天壽山。

translations.literal: The Embroidered Uniform Guard centurion Sui Quan and the Directorate of Imperial Entertainments clerk Qian Zixun, having already been stripped of office for crimes, sought favor by requesting that the Xian Emperor's coffin at Xianling be moved north for burial at Tianshou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The Embroidered Uniform Guard centurion Sui Quan and the Directorate of Imperial Entertainments clerk Qian Zixun, having already been stripped of office for crimes, sought favor by requesting that the Xian Emperor's coffin at Xianling be moved north for burial at Tianshou Mountain.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書趙璜等斥其謬，帝復下廷議。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhao Huang and others denounced this as absurd, and the emperor again submitted it to court debate.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zhao Huang and others denounced this as absurd, and the emperor again submitted it to court debate.

sentences.zh: 書乃會廷臣上言：「顯陵，先帝體魄所藏，不可輕動。

translations.literal: Shu then convened the court officials and submitted a memorial saying: "Xianling is where the late emperor's remains are buried and must not be lightly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Shu then convened the court officials and submitted a memorial saying: "Xianling is where the late emperor's remains are buried and must not be lightly disturbed.

sentences.zh: 昔高皇帝不遷祖陵，文皇帝不遷孝陵。

translations.literal: Formerly the Founding Emperor did not move the ancestral tombs, and Emperor Wen did not move Xiaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Founding Emperor did not move the ancestral tombs, and Emperor Wen did not move Xiaoling.

sentences.zh: 全等諂諛小人，妄論山陵，宜下法司按問。」

translations.literal: Quan and the others are sycophantic petty men who recklessly discuss imperial tombs and should be handed to the judicial offices for investigation."
translations.idiomatic: Quan and the others are sycophantic petty men who recklessly discuss imperial tombs and should be handed to the judicial offices for investigation."

sentences.zh: 帝報曰：「先帝陵寢在遠，朕朝夕思望，不勝哀痛，其再詳議以聞。」

translations.literal: The emperor replied: "The late emperor's tomb is far away; I think of it morning and evening and cannot overcome my grief. Debate this again in detail and report."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "The late emperor's tomb is far away; I think of it morning and evening and cannot overcome my grief. Debate this again in detail and report."

sentences.zh: 書復集眾議，極言不可，乃已。

translations.literal: Shu again gathered everyone for debate and argued forcefully that it could not be done, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Shu again gathered everyone for debate and argued forcefully that it could not be done, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 書以「大禮」告成，宜有以答天下望，乃條新政十二事以獻，帝優旨報焉。

translations.literal: Shu, holding that the "Great Rites" were complete and that something should answer the realm's expectations, listed twelve items of new policy and presented them; the emperor responded with gracious approval.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, holding that the "Great Rites" were complete and that something should answer the realm's expectations, listed twelve items of new policy and presented them; the emperor responded with gracious approval.

sentences.zh: 大同軍變，殺巡撫張文錦，毀總兵官江桓印，而出故帥朱振於獄，令代桓。

translations.literal: When the Datong garrison mutinied, they killed Grand Coordinator Zhang Wenjin, destroyed the seal of Regional Commander Jiang Huan, released the former commander Zhu Zhen from prison, and made him replace Huan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Datong garrison mutinied, they killed Grand Coordinator Zhang Wenjin, destroyed the seal of Regional Commander Jiang Huan, released the former commander Zhu Zhen from prison, and made him replace Huan.

sentences.zh: 帝因而命之，諭禮部鑄新印。

translations.literal: The emperor accordingly confirmed the appointment and ordered the Ministry of Rites to cast a new seal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accordingly confirmed the appointment and ordered the Ministry of Rites to cast a new seal.

sentences.zh: 書持不可，請討之，與政府忤。

translations.literal: Shu held that this could not be allowed and requested a punitive campaign, clashing with the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Shu held that this could not be allowed and requested a punitive campaign, clashing with the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 時執政者費宏、石缶、賈詠，書心弗善也，乃力薦楊一清、王守仁入閣，且曰：「今諸大臣皆中材，無足與計天下事。

translations.literal: At that time those wielding power were Fei Hong, Shi Zong, and Jia Yong; in his heart Shu was displeased, and so he vigorously recommended Yang Yiqing and Wang Shouren to enter the Grand Secretariat, saying furthermore: "Today's various great ministers are all middling talent, not sufficient to consult with on affairs under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the men in power were Fei Hong, Shi Zong, and Jia Yong; Shu disapproved of them and vigorously pushed to bring Yang Yiqing and Wang Shouren into the Grand Secretariat, saying: "Today's senior ministers are all mediocre—none of them are fit to deliberate on the affairs of the realm.

sentences.zh: 定亂濟時，非守仁不可。」

translations.literal: To settle disorder and succor the age, none but Shouren will do."
translations.idiomatic: To quell rebellion and rescue the times, no one but Shouren will suffice."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「書為大臣，當抒猷略，共濟時艱，何以中材自諉。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Shu, as a great minister, ought to set forth plans and strategies and together relieve the hardships of the age—why excuse yourself with 'middling talent'?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Shu, as a senior minister, should put forward your counsel and share in relieving the empire's distress—why plead mediocrity as an excuse?"

sentences.zh: 守仁迄不獲柄用。

translations.literal: Shouren ultimately never obtained practical appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouren never gained effective power.

sentences.zh: 四年，光祿寺丞何淵請建世室，祀獻皇帝於太廟。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, He Yuan, assistant director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, requested construction of an Eternal Shrine to sacrifice to Emperor Xian in the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, He Yuan, assistant director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, petitioned to establish an Eternal Shrine and sacrifice to Emperor Xian in the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 帝命禮官集議，書等上議；

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the ritual officials to assemble for deliberation; Shu and others submitted their opinion;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the ritual officials to confer; Shu and others submitted a memorial of opinion:

sentences.zh: 「《王制》：『天子七廟，三昭三穆』。

translations.literal: "The Rites of Zhou states: 'The Son of Heaven has seven temples—three zhao and three mu.
translations.idiomatic: "The Rites of Zhou says: 'The Son of Heaven has seven temples—three zhao and three mu.

sentences.zh: 周以文、武有大功德，乃立世室，與後稷廟皆百世不遷。

translations.literal: Zhou, because Wen and Wu had great merit and virtue, established Eternal Shrines, which together with the temple of Hou Ji were never moved for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Because King Wen and King Wu of Zhou had achieved great merit, the Zhou established Eternal Shrines; these, together with the temple of Hou Ji, were never displaced for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 我太祖立四親廟，德祖居北，後改同堂異室。

translations.literal: Our Taizu established four temples for his four forebears, with Dezu in the north; later this was changed to one hall with separate chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Our founding emperor established four temples for his four immediate ancestors, with Dezu placed to the north; this was later changed to a single hall with separate chambers.

sentences.zh: 議祧則以太祖擬文世室，太宗擬武世室。

translations.literal: In deliberating on ancestral supersession, Taizu was taken as parallel to Wen's Eternal Shrine and Taizong to Wu's Eternal Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: When the question of temple supersession was debated, Taizu was treated as equivalent to Wen's Eternal Shrine and Taizong to Wu's.

sentences.zh: 今獻皇帝以藩王追崇帝號，何淵乃欲比之太祖、太宗，立世室於太廟，甚無據。」

translations.literal: Now Emperor Xian was posthumously ennobled with an imperial title from his status as a princely son; He Yuan yet wishes to compare him to the Taizu and Taizong and establish an Eternal Shrine in the Grand Ancestral Temple—this is utterly without basis."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xian was posthumously elevated from princely rank to an imperial title; for He Yuan to compare him with the Taizu and Taizong and install an Eternal Shrine in the Grand Ancestral Temple is wholly without precedent."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was issued.
translations.idiomatic: No reply was given.

sentences.zh: 頃之，張璁特奏上，力言不可，書亦三疏如璁議。

translations.literal: Before long Zhang Cong submitted a special memorial, forcefully arguing that it could not be done; Shu also submitted three memorials in accord with Cong's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhang Cong submitted a special memorial vigorously opposing the plan; Shu likewise submitted three memorials echoing Cong's position.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中官即其家諭之，書復密疏切諫。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a palace eunuch to his home to instruct him; Shu again submitted a secret memorial with forceful remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace eunuch to Shu's home to instruct him, but Shu submitted another secret memorial of urgent remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，責以畏眾飾奸。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and rebuked him for fearing the multitude and covering up wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and rebuked him for bowing to public opinion and shielding wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 乃議別立禰廟，而世室之議竟寢。

translations.literal: They then deliberated on establishing a separate temple to his father, and the proposal for an Eternal Shrine was ultimately abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The court then debated establishing a separate temple for the emperor's father, and the Eternal Shrine proposal was finally dropped.

sentences.zh: 五年秋，章聖太后將謁世廟，禮官議不合。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year, Empress Zhangsheng was about to visit the imperial ancestral temple; the ritual officials' deliberations did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifth year, Empress Zhangsheng planned to visit the imperial ancestral temple, but the ritual officials could not agree on the proper procedure.

sentences.zh: 書以目眚在告，上言：「母後謁廟，事出創聞，禮官實無所據，惟聖明裁酌。

translations.literal: Shu, citing an eye ailment, took leave and submitted a memorial: "The empress dowager's visit to the temple is unprecedented; the ritual officials truly have no precedent to rely on—only Your Majesty's sagacious judgment can decide.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, pleading an eye ailment, took leave and memorialized: "An empress dowager's visit to the temple is without precedent; the ritual officials truly have no authority to cite—only Your Majesty's wise judgment can decide.

sentences.zh: 且世廟既成，宜有肆赦之典，請盡還議禮遣戍諸臣。

translations.literal: Moreover, since the imperial ancestral temple is already complete, there should be a general amnesty; I request that all officials banished for debating the rites be fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, now that the imperial ancestral temple is complete, a general amnesty is fitting; I beg that all officials exiled for debating the rites be fully restored.

sentences.zh: 所謂合萬國之歡心以祀先王，此天子大孝也。」

translations.literal: What is called joining the joy of all the states to sacrifice to the former kings—this is the Son of Heaven's supreme filial piety."
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by uniting the hearts of all the realm in joy to sacrifice to the former kings—the Son of Heaven's supreme filial piety."

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: The report was acknowledged.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was noted.

sentences.zh: 書以議禮受帝知，倚為親臣。

translations.literal: Shu, because of his role in debating the rites, gained the emperor's trust and was relied upon as an intimate minister.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his work on the rites debate, Shu won the emperor's confidence and was treated as a trusted intimate.

sentences.zh: 初進《大禮集議》，加太子太保，尋以《獻帝實錄》成，進少保。

translations.literal: Upon first submitting the Collected Debates on the Great Rites, he was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; soon after the Veritable Record of Emperor Xian was completed, he was promoted to Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When he first presented the Collected Debates on the Great Rites, he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; soon after the Veritable Record of Emperor Xian was completed, he was promoted to Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 眷顧隆異，雖諸輔臣莫敢望。

translations.literal: Imperial favor was lofty and extraordinary; even the chief ministers dared not compare.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial favor toward him was extraordinary; even the chief ministers could not hope to match it.

sentences.zh: 而書得疾不能視事，屢疏乞休，舉羅欽順自代，帝輒慰留不允。

translations.literal: But Shu fell ill and could not attend to affairs; he repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement and recommended Luo Qinshun to succeed him; the emperor always comforted him and refused to allow it.
translations.idiomatic: But Shu fell ill and could no longer manage affairs; he repeatedly petitioned to retire and recommended Luo Qinshun as his successor, yet the emperor always comforted him and refused.

sentences.zh: 其後疾篤，請益力，詔加武英殿大學士，賜第京師，支俸如故。

translations.literal: Later his illness grew grave and his requests became more forceful; an edict promoted him to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Martial Glory, granted him a residence in the capital, and continued his salary as before.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness worsened and his pleas grew more urgent, an edict made him Grand Secretary of the Hall of Martial Glory, granted him a residence in the capital, and continued his salary unchanged.

sentences.zh: 甫聞命而卒。

translations.literal: He had just received the appointment when he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the moment he received the appointment.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，謚文襄，任一子尚寶丞，異數也。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title Grand Preceptor, with the posthumous name Wenxiang; one son was appointed Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Seals—exceptional honors.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Grand Preceptor with the posthumous name Wenxiang; one son was appointed Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Seals—honors far beyond the norm.

sentences.zh: 書遇事敢為，性頗偏愎。

translations.literal: Shu was bold in action when facing affairs; by nature he was rather obstinate and wilful.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was bold in action but by nature rather stubborn and wilful.

sentences.zh: 初，長沙人李鑒為盜，知府宋卿論之死。

translations.literal: Earlier, one Li Jian of Changsha was a bandit; Prefect Song Qing sentenced him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a man of Changsha named Li Jian had turned bandit; Prefect Song Qing sentenced him to death.

sentences.zh: 書方巡撫湖廣，發卿贓私，因劾卿故入鑒罪。

translations.literal: Shu was then grand coordinator of Huguang; he exposed Qing's corruption and private wrongdoing, and therefore impeached Qing for deliberately inflating Jian's guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was then grand coordinator of Huguang; he uncovered Qing's corruption and impeached him for deliberately aggravating Jian's crime.

sentences.zh: 帝遣大臣按，不如書言。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched a great minister to investigate; the findings did not match Shu's claims.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a senior minister to investigate, but the findings did not bear out Shu's accusations.

sentences.zh: 而書時已得幸，乃命逮鑒入京再訊。

translations.literal: But by then Shu was already in favor, so the emperor ordered Jian seized and brought to the capital for re-examination.
translations.idiomatic: But Shu was already in favor by then, so the emperor ordered Li Jian seized and brought to the capital for retrial.

sentences.zh: 書遂言：「臣以議禮犯眾怒，故刑官率右卿而重鑒罪，請敕法司辨雪。」

translations.literal: Shu then said: "Your servant, having angered the multitude through debating the rites, therefore the judicial officials uniformly sided with Qing and aggravated Jian's guilt; I request an edict ordering the judicial authorities to investigate and clear the matter."
translations.idiomatic: Shu then said: "Your servant provoked widespread anger through the rites debate, and so the judicial officials sided with Qing and inflated Jian's guilt; I beg that Your Majesty order the judicial authorities to investigate and clear the injustice."

sentences.zh: 及法司讞上無異詞，帝重違書意，特減鑒死遣戍。

translations.literal: When the judicial authorities submitted their final judgment without dissent, the emperor greatly feared violating Shu's wishes and specially commuted Jian's death sentence to banishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the judicial authorities submitted their verdict without dissent, the emperor, reluctant to go against Shu's wishes, specially commuted Jian's death sentence to exile.

sentences.zh: 其他庇陳洸，排費宏，率恣行私意，為時論所斥。

translations.literal: In other matters he shielded Chen Huan, attacked Fei Hong, and generally acted at will for private ends—matters for which contemporaries condemned him.
translations.idiomatic: He also shielded Chen Huan, attacked Fei Hong, and generally acted on private whim—conduct for which public opinion condemned him.

sentences.zh: 弟春、篆。

translations.literal: (younger brother Chunzhuan)]〉
translations.idiomatic: (younger brother Chunzhuan)]〉

sentences.zh: 春由庶吉士授御史，巡雲南。

translations.literal: Chun, from his position as a Hanlin bachelor, was appointed censor and toured Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Chun, having served as a Hanlin bachelor, was appointed censor and sent to inspect Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 以兄為都御史，改翰林檢討。

translations.literal: Because his elder brother was censor-in-chief, he was transferred to Hanlin Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Because his elder brother was censor-in-chief, he was reassigned to the post of Hanlin Reviser.

sentences.zh: 預修《武宗實錄》成，當進秩。

translations.literal: Having assisted in compiling the Veritable Record of Emperor Wuzong to completion, he was due for promotion in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Having helped compile the Veritable Record of Emperor Wuzong to completion, he was due for promotion.

sentences.zh: 內閣費宏以春由他官入，與檢討劉夔並擬按察僉事。

translations.literal: Fei Hong of the Grand Secretariat, on the grounds that Chun had entered from another office, together with Reviser Liu Kui both proposed appointing them as Assistant Surveillance Commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Hong of the Grand Secretariat, holding that Chun had entered the Hanlin from another track, together with Reviser Liu Kui proposed appointing both men as assistant surveillance commissioners.

sentences.zh: 夔亦故御史，以避兄侍郎龍改授者也。

translations.literal: Kui was also formerly a censor, re-assigned to avoid his elder brother, Vice Minister Long.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was also a former censor, reassigned to the Hanlin to avoid serving alongside his elder brother, Vice Minister Long.

sentences.zh: 書大怒，疏言：「故事，無纂修書成出為外任者。」

translations.literal: Shu was furious and memorialized: "By precedent, none who completed compilation of a historical work have been sent out to provincial posts."
translations.idiomatic: Shu was furious and memorialized: "By precedent, no one who completed a compilation assignment has been sent out to a provincial post."

sentences.zh: 帝以書故留春，擢修撰，而夔亦留，擢編修。

translations.literal: The emperor for Shu's sake retained Chun, promoting him to Compiler, and Kui was also retained, promoted to Editor.
translations.idiomatic: For Shu's sake the emperor kept Chun and promoted him to Compiler; Kui was also retained and promoted to Editor.

sentences.zh: 書由是怨宏，數詆諆。

translations.literal: Shu thereby came to resent Hong and repeatedly slandered and defamed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shu thereafter bore a grudge against Hong and repeatedly slandered him.

sentences.zh: 及書卒，帝念其議禮功，累進春翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Shu died, the emperor remembered his merit in debating the rites and repeatedly promoted Chun to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu died, the emperor remembered his service in the rites debate and repeatedly promoted Chun until he became a Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十二年由禮部右侍郎改吏部。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Jiajing he was transferred from Vice Minister of Rites to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Jiajing he was moved from Vice Minister of Rites to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 詔舉堪翰林者，春欲召還故翰林楊惟聰、陳沂，尚書汪鋐不可，遂有隙。

translations.literal: An edict called for recommending those qualified for the Hanlin; Chun wished to recall former Hanlin scholars Yang Weicong and Chen Yi, but Minister Wang Qian objected, and thereupon a rift arose.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict called for recommending men fit for the Hanlin, Chun wished to recall former Hanlin scholars Yang Weicong and Chen Yi, but Minister Wang Qian refused, and a rift opened between them.

sentences.zh: 後鋐有所推舉，不與春議，春怒詬鋐。

translations.literal: Later when Qian had someone to recommend, he did not consult Chun; Chun angrily reviled Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Qian had candidates to recommend, he did not consult Chun; Chun flew into a rage and cursed Qian.

sentences.zh: 鋐訐春前附楊廷和排議禮諸臣，遂落職。

translations.literal: Qian impeached Chun for having earlier attached himself to Yang Tinghe and oppressed the officials who debated the rites; Chun was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Qian impeached Chun for having once sided with Yang Tinghe in persecuting the officials who debated the rites, and Chun was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 篆為戶科給事中。

translations.literal: Zhuan served as a supervising secretary in the Household Section.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuan served as a supervising secretary in the Household Section.

sentences.zh: 黔國公沐昆劾按察使沈恩等，篆與同官李長私語昆奏多誣，長即劾昆。

translations.literal: Duke of Qian Mu Kun impeached Surveillance Commissioner Shen En and others; Zhuan privately told fellow official Li Chang that Kun's memorial contained much falsehood, and Chang immediately impeached Kun.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Qian, Mu Kun, impeached Surveillance Commissioner Shen En and others; Zhuan privately told his colleague Li Chang that Kun's memorial was largely false, and Chang immediately impeached Kun in turn.

sentences.zh: 武宗責長誣重臣，下詔獄。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong rebuked Chang for slandering a high minister and had him imprisoned in the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong rebuked Chang for slandering a senior minister and had him thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 詞連篆，並系治謫外，篆得夷陵判官。

translations.literal: The case implicated Zhuan; both were imprisoned, tried, and banished to peripheral posts; Zhuan received the post of assistant magistrate of Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: The case implicated Zhuan as well; both men were imprisoned, tried, and banished; Zhuan was given the post of assistant magistrate of Yiling.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，復故官，未上卒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne, his former office was restored, but before he took up the post he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, Zhuan's former office was restored, but he died before he could take it up.

sentences.zh: 予祭，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Sacrifices were granted, and he was posthumously given Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices were granted, and he was posthumously ennobled as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 霍韜，字渭先，南海人。

translations.literal: Huo Tao, styled Weixian, was a native of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Tao, styled Weixian, was a native of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 舉正德九年會試第一。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhengde he placed first in the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhengde he ranked first in the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 謁歸成婚，讀書西樵山，經史淹洽。

translations.literal: He returned home to marry, studied on Mount Xiqiao, and was thoroughly versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to marry, studied on Mount Xiqiao, and became thoroughly versed in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 世宗踐阼，除職方主事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, he was appointed secretary in the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, he was appointed secretary in the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 楊廷和方柄政，韜上言：「閣臣職參機務，今止票擬，而裁決歸近習。

translations.literal: Yang Tinghe was then wielding power; Tao submitted a memorial saying: "Grand secretaries' duty is to participate in state affairs; today they only draft rescripts while decisions rest with those near the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tinghe was then in power; Tao memorialized: "Grand secretaries are charged with sharing in state affairs, yet today they merely draft rescripts while real decisions rest with those close to the throne.

sentences.zh: 輔臣失參贊之權，近習起幹政之漸。

translations.literal: The chief ministers lost the power to assist and advise; those near the throne began the first steps toward meddling in government.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers have lost the power to counsel, while those near the throne have begun to encroach on governance.

sentences.zh: 自今章奏，請召大臣面決施行，講官、臺諫，班列左右，眾議而公駁之。

translations.literal: From now on, for memorials and reports, please summon the great ministers to decide face to face before implementation; lecturers and censorial remonstrators should stand in rows to left and right—debate publicly and refute openly.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, when memorials arrive, summon the senior ministers to decide them face to face before execution; let lecturers and censorial remonstrators stand in ranks to either side, debate openly, and rebut in public.

sentences.zh: 宰相得取善之名，內臣免招權之謗。」

translations.literal: The chief minister would gain the reputation of accepting good counsel, and inner-court eunuchs would avoid the reproach of monopolizing power."
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister would gain credit for accepting good counsel, and inner-court eunuchs would escape the charge of usurping power."

sentences.zh: 因言錦衣不當典刑獄，東廠不當預朝議，撫按兵備官不當以軍功授秩蔭，興府護衛軍不當盡取入京概授官職，御史謝源、伍希儒赴難有功不當罷黜，平逆藩功自安慶、南昌外，不當濫敘。

translations.literal: He further argued that the Embroidered-Uniform Guard should not administer criminal prisons, the Eastern Depot should not participate in court deliberations, grand coordinators and military preparedness officials should not receive ranks and hereditary privileges for military merit, the Prince of Xing's guard troops should not all be brought to the capital and indiscriminately granted offices, Censors Xie Yuan and Wu Xiru should not be dismissed after meritorious service in the crisis, and merit in suppressing the rebellious fief should not be broadly rewarded except for those at Anqing and Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: He further argued that the Embroidered-Uniform Guard should not run criminal prisons; the Eastern Depot should not join court deliberations; grand coordinators and military preparedness officials should not receive ranks and hereditary privileges for military merit; the Prince of Xing's guard should not all be brought to the capital and given offices indiscriminately; Censors Xie Yuan and Wu Xiru, who had served meritoriously in the crisis, should not be dismissed; and rewards for suppressing the rebellious fief should not be handed out broadly beyond those who fought at Anqing and Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 及「大禮」議起，禮部尚書毛澄力持考孝宗，韜私為《大禮議》駁之。

translations.literal: When the debate over the "Great Rites" arose, Minister of Rites Mao Cheng staunchly held that the emperor should treat Xiaozong as his father; Tao privately composed the Debates on the Great Rites to refute this.
translations.idiomatic: When the "Great Rites" debate arose, Minister of Rites Mao Cheng staunchly held that the emperor should treat Xiaozong as his father; Tao privately wrote the Debates on the Great Rites to refute him.

sentences.zh: 澄貽書相質難，韜三上書極辨其非。

translations.literal: Cheng sent a letter questioning him in debate; Tao three times submitted memorials vigorously arguing against Cheng's position.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng sent a letter challenging him; Tao submitted three memorials vigorously rebutting Cheng's position.

sentences.zh: 已，知澄意不可回，其年十月上疏曰：

translations.literal: Later, knowing Cheng's mind could not be turned, in the tenth month of that year he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Later, seeing that Cheng's mind could not be changed, in the tenth month of that year he submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 按廷議謂陛下宜以孝宗為父，興獻王為叔，別擇崇仁王子為獻王後，考之古禮則不合，質之聖賢之道則不通，揆之今日之事體則不順。

translations.literal: According to court deliberation, Your Majesty should take Xiaozong as your father, the Prince of Xing as your uncle, and separately select a son of the Prince of Chongren to succeed the Prince of Xing as his heir—examined against ancient rites this does not accord; tested against the way of the sages it does not hold; measured against the circumstances of today it is not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: According to court deliberation, Your Majesty should take Xiaozong as your father, the Prince of Xing as your uncle, and separately choose a son of the Prince of Chongren to succeed the Prince of Xing—examined against ancient rites this does not accord; tested against the way of the sages it does not hold; measured against present circumstances it is not fitting.

sentences.zh: 考《儀禮·喪服》章雲「斬衰為所後者」。

translations.literal: Examining the chapter on mourning dress in the Book of Etiquette and Ceremonial - Mourning Dress, it says: "The unhemmed sackcloth is worn for the one to whom one succeeds as heir."
translations.idiomatic: The chapter on mourning dress in the Book of Etiquette and Ceremonial - Mourning Dress says: "The unhemmed sackcloth mourning is worn for the one to whom one succeeds as heir."

sentences.zh: 又雲「為人後者，為其父母報」。

translations.literal: It also says: "One who becomes another's heir still wears mourning for his natural parents."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "One who becomes another's heir still observes mourning for his natural parents."

sentences.zh: 是於所後者，蓋無稱為父母之說，而於本生父母又無改稱伯叔父母之雲也。

translations.literal: Thus regarding the one to whom one succeeds as heir, there is surely no doctrine of calling him father; and regarding one's natural-born parents, there is likewise no mention of changing to call them uncle and aunt.
translations.idiomatic: Thus toward the one to whom one succeeds as heir, there is no doctrine of calling him father; and toward one's natural-born parents, there is no mention of changing to call them uncle and aunt.

sentences.zh: 漢儒不明其義，謬為邪說曰「為人後者為之子」。

translations.literal: Han Confucians did not understand the meaning and wrongly devised a heterodox doctrine saying: "One who becomes another's heir becomes that person's son."
translations.idiomatic: Han Confucians failed to grasp the meaning and wrongly devised a heterodox doctrine: "One who becomes another's heir becomes that person's son."

sentences.zh: 果如其言，則漢宣帝當為昭帝後矣。

translations.literal: If that doctrine were true, then Emperor Xuan of Han ought to have been Zhao's heir.
translations.idiomatic: If that doctrine were true, then Emperor Xuan of Han ought to have been Emperor Zhao's heir.

sentences.zh: 然昭帝從祖也，宣帝從孫也，孫將謂祖為父，可乎？

translations.literal: Yet Zhao was Xuan's granduncle, and Xuan was Zhao's grandnephew—could a grandson call his granduncle father?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhao was Xuan's granduncle and Xuan was Zhao's grandnephew—could a grandson call his granduncle father?

sentences.zh: 唐宣宗當為武宗後矣，然武宗侄也，宣宗叔也，叔反謂侄為父，可乎？

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong of Tang ought to have been Wuzong's heir; yet Wuzong was Xuanzong's nephew and Xuanzong Wuzong's uncle—could an uncle call his nephew father?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong of Tang ought to have been Wuzong's heir; yet Wuzong was Xuanzong's nephew and Xuanzong was Wuzong's uncle—could an uncle call his nephew father?

sentences.zh: 吳諸樊兄弟四人以國相授受，蓋叠相為後矣，是兄弟自具高曾祖考也，而可乎？

translations.literal: The four brothers of the Zhu Fan clan of Wu handed the state among themselves, each in turn becoming another's heir—in effect brothers possessed their own great-grandfather, grandfather, and father; could that be?
translations.idiomatic: The four Zhu Fan brothers of Wu handed the state among themselves, each in turn becoming another's heir—in effect brothers supplied their own great-grandfather, grandfather, and father; could that be?

sentences.zh: 故曰考之古禮則不合也。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: examined against ancient rites, it does not accord.
translations.idiomatic: Hence it is said: examined against ancient rites, it does not accord.

sentences.zh: 天下者，天下之天下，非一人所得私也。

translations.literal: All under Heaven is the All-under-Heaven of all under Heaven—not something one person may claim privately.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven belongs to all under Heaven—it is not something one person may treat as private property.

sentences.zh: 宋人之告其君曰：「仁宗於宗室中特簡聖明，授以大業，陛下所以負扆端冕，富有四海，子孫萬世相承，皆先帝之德。」

translations.literal: A Song man told his ruler: "Emperor Renzong, choosing the most sagacious among the imperial clan, bestowed the great enterprise upon him—Your Majesty therefore sits upon the throne draped in authority, possesses all within the four seas, and your descendants inherit for ten thousand generations—all the virtue of the former emperor."
translations.idiomatic: A Song official told his ruler: "Emperor Renzong, selecting the most sagacious among the imperial clan, bestowed the great enterprise upon him—Your Majesty therefore sits upon the throne in full regalia, holds all within the four seas, and your descendants inherit for ten thousand generations—all through the virtue of the former emperor."

sentences.zh: 蓋謂仁宗以天下授英宗，宜舍本生父母而以仁宗為父母也。

translations.literal: This meant that since Renzong bestowed All-under-Heaven upon Yingzong, one ought to abandon one's natural-born parents and take Renzong as one's parents.
translations.idiomatic: This meant that because Renzong bestowed the realm upon Yingzong, one ought to abandon one's natural-born parents and treat Renzong as one's parents.

sentences.zh: 臣以聖賢之道觀之，孟子言舜為天子，瞽瞍殺人，臯陶執之，舜則竊負而逃，是父母重而天下輕也。

translations.literal: Examined by the way of the sages, Mencius said that when Shun became Son of Heaven, if his father Gusou committed murder, Gao Yao would arrest him, and Shun would secretly carry him on his back and flee—this is parents being weighty and All-under-Heaven being light.
translations.idiomatic: Viewed through the way of the sages, Mencius said that when Shun became Son of Heaven, if his father Gusou committed murder, Gao Yao would arrest him, and Shun would secretly carry him on his back and flee—this shows that parents outweigh the realm.

sentences.zh: 若宋儒之說，則天下重而父母輕矣。

translations.literal: If the doctrine of the Song Confucians holds, then All-under-Heaven is weighty and parents are light.
translations.idiomatic: If the Song Confucians' doctrine holds, then the realm outweighs one's parents.

sentences.zh: 故曰求之聖賢之道則不通也。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: tested against the way of the sages, it does not hold.
translations.idiomatic: Hence it is said: tested against the way of the sages, it does not hold.

sentences.zh: 武宗嗣孝宗歷十有六年，考宗非無嗣也。

translations.literal: Wuzong succeeded Xiaozong and reigned for sixteen years—Xiaozong was not without a successor.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong succeeded Xiaozong and reigned for sixteen years—Xiaozong was not without an heir.

sentences.zh: 今強欲陛下重為孝宗之嗣，何為也哉？

translations.literal: Now to force Your Majesty to become Xiaozong's successor again—what is the purpose?
translations.idiomatic: Now to force Your Majesty to become Xiaozong's heir anew—what is the point?

sentences.zh: 夫陛下為孝宗子矣，誰為武宗子乎？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty is Xiaozong's son, then who is Wuzong's son?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty is Xiaozong's son, then who is Wuzong's son?

sentences.zh: 孝宗有兩嗣子矣，武宗獨無嗣子，可乎？

translations.literal: Xiaozong would have two successors, while Wuzong alone would have none—can that be?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong would have two heirs while Wuzong alone would have none—can that be?

sentences.zh: 臣子於君父一也，既不忍孝宗之無嗣，獨忍武宗之無嗣乎？

translations.literal: Ministers and subjects toward their lord and father are one and the same: since you cannot bear that Xiaozong be without a successor, can you alone bear that Wuzong be without a successor?
translations.idiomatic: A subject's duty to his lord is like a son's to his father: if you cannot bear that Xiaozong be without an heir, can you alone bear that Wuzong be without one?

sentences.zh: 若曰武宗以兄，固得享弟之祀，則孝宗以伯，獨不得享侄之祀乎？

translations.literal: If it is said that Wuzong, as elder brother, may naturally receive his younger brother's sacrifices, then Xiaozong, as uncle, may he alone not receive his nephew's sacrifices?
translations.idiomatic: If Wuzong, as elder brother, may naturally receive his younger brother's sacrifices, then may Xiaozong, as uncle, alone be denied his nephew's sacrifices?

sentences.zh: 既可越武宗直繼孝宗矣，獨不可並越孝宗直繼憲宗乎？

translations.literal: If one may skip over Wuzong to succeed Xiaozong directly, may one not also skip over Xiaozong to succeed Xianzong directly?
translations.idiomatic: If one may skip over Wuzong to succeed Xiaozong directly, why may one not also skip over Xiaozong to succeed Xianzong directly?

sentences.zh: 武宗無嗣，無可如何矣。

translations.literal: That Wuzong had no successor—nothing can be done about that.
translations.idiomatic: That Wuzong had no heir—nothing can be done about that.

sentences.zh: 孝宗有嗣，復強繼其嗣，而絕興獻之嗣，是於孝宗無所益，而於興獻不大有損乎？

translations.literal: That Xiaozong had a successor yet you would force him to take another, while cutting off the succession of the Prince of Xing—this benefits Xiaozong in no way, yet greatly damages the Prince of Xing, does it not?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong already had an heir, yet you would force another upon him while cutting off the Prince of Xing's line—this benefits Xiaozong not at all while greatly harming the Prince of Xing, does it not?

sentences.zh: 故曰揆之今日之事體則不順也。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: measured against the circumstances of today, it is not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Hence it is said: measured against present circumstances, it is not fitting.

sentences.zh: 然臣下之為此議也，其故有三：曰前代故事之拘也，曰不忘孝宗之德也，曰避迎合之嫌也。

translations.literal: Yet the reasons why your officials make this proposal are three: being bound by precedents of former ages; not forgetting Xiaozong's virtue; and avoiding the suspicion of currying favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the reasons your officials advance this proposal are three: clinging to precedents of former ages; not forgetting Xiaozong's virtue; and avoiding the suspicion of currying favor.

sentences.zh: 今陛下既考孝宗矣，尊興獻王以帝號矣，則將如斯而已乎？

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has already treated Xiaozong as father and honored the Prince of Xing with an imperial title—will it end at only this?
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has already treated Xiaozong as father and honored the Prince of Xing with an imperial title—is that all there is to it?

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂帝王之相繼也，繼其統而已矣，固不屑屑於父子之稱也。

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to hold that when emperors succeed one another, they succeed only to the lineage—they need not fuss over the appellation of father and son.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that when emperors succeed one another, they succeed only to the lineage—they need not quibble over the names of father and son.

sentences.zh: 惟繼其統，則不惟孝宗之統不絕，即武宗之統亦不絕矣。

translations.literal: If one succeeds only to the lineage, then not only is Xiaozong's lineage not cut off—the lineage of Wuzong too is not cut off.
translations.idiomatic: If one succeeds only to the lineage, then not only is Xiaozong's line preserved—Wuzong's line is preserved as well.

sentences.zh: 然則如之何而可乎？

translations.literal: Then what must be done for it to be acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Then what must be done to set things right?

sentences.zh: 惟陛下於興獻王得正父子之稱，以不絕天性之恩。

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty obtains the proper father-son designation toward the Prince of Xing can the bond of natural affection not be severed.
translations.idiomatic: Only if Your Majesty secures the proper father-son designation for the Prince of Xing can the bond of natural affection remain intact.

sentences.zh: 於國母之迎，得正天子之母之禮。

translations.literal: In welcoming the emperor's mother, obtain the proper rites due the mother of the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In welcoming the emperor's mother, observe the proper rites owed to the mother of the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 復於昭聖太后、武宗皇后處之有其道，事之盡其誠，則於尊尊親親兩不悖矣。

translations.literal: Furthermore, if toward Empress Dowager Zhaosheng and Empress Zhuangsu one conducts oneself with proper principle and serves them with utmost sincerity, then in honoring the honored and cherishing the kin, neither will be violated.
translations.idiomatic: If toward Empress Dowager Zhaosheng and Empress Zhuangsu one acts with proper principle and serves them with full sincerity, then in honoring the honored and cherishing kin, neither duty will be violated.

sentences.zh: 帝得疏喜甚，迫群議不遽行。

translations.literal: The emperor, upon receiving the memorial, was greatly pleased, but constrained by the assembled deliberations, did not immediately act on it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased upon receiving the memorial, but constrained by the assembled deliberations, he did not act on it at once.

sentences.zh: 而朝士鹹指目韜為邪說。

translations.literal: Court officials all pointed at Tao as peddling heterodox doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials all pointed at Tao as peddling heretical doctrine.

sentences.zh: 韜意不自得，尋謝病歸。

translations.literal: Tao felt ill at ease and soon resigned citing illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Tao felt ill at ease and soon resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年，帝議尊崇所生益急，兩詔召韜。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing, as the emperor's deliberations to honor his biological father grew more urgent, he twice issued edicts summoning Tao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiajing, as the emperor's plans to honor his biological father grew more urgent, he twice issued edicts summoning Tao.

sentences.zh: 韜辭疾不赴，馳疏言：

translations.literal: Tao declined on grounds of illness and did not come; he rushed a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tao pleaded illness and did not come; he hurriedly submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 今日大禮之議，兩端而已。

translations.literal: "Today's debate over the Great Rites has only two directions.
translations.idiomatic: "Today's debate over the Great Rites has only two sides.

sentences.zh: 曰崇正統之大義也，曰正天倫之大經也。

translations.literal: One is to uphold the great principle of the legitimate succession; one is to set right the great constant of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: One upholds the great principle of legitimate succession; one sets right the great constant of human relations.

sentences.zh: 徒尊正統，其弊至於利天下而棄父母；

translations.literal: If one honors only the legitimate succession, the harm may reach the point of benefiting the realm while abandoning one's parents;
translations.idiomatic: Honor only the legitimate succession, and the harm may reach the point of benefiting the realm while abandoning one's parents;

sentences.zh: 徒重天倫，其弊至於小加大而卑逾尊。

translations.literal: If one values only human relations, the harm may reach the point of the lesser overriding the greater and the base exceeding the honored.
translations.idiomatic: Value only human relations, and the harm may reach the point of the lesser overriding the greater and the base exceeding the honored.

sentences.zh: 故臣謂陛下宜稱孝宗曰皇伯考，獻帝曰皇考。

translations.literal: Therefore your servant holds that Your Majesty ought to address Xiaozong as Imperial Uncle-Father and address Emperor Xian as Imperial Father.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore your servant holds that Your Majesty should address Xiaozong as Imperial Uncle-Father and Emperor Xian as Imperial Father.

sentences.zh: 此天倫之當辨者也。

translations.literal: This is what ought to be distinguished in human relations.
translations.idiomatic: This is what must be distinguished in human relations.

sentences.zh: 尊崇之議，則姑在所緩，此大統之當崇者也。

translations.literal: The debate over enhanced honors may for the present be set aside; this is what ought to be revered regarding the great succession.
translations.idiomatic: The debate over enhanced honors may for now be deferred; this is what must be upheld regarding the great succession.

sentences.zh: 乃廷議欲陛下上考孝宗，又兼考獻帝，此漢人兩統之失也。

translations.literal: Yet court deliberation wishes Your Majesty to treat Xiaozong as father above and also treat Emperor Xian as father—this is the Han error of dual successions.
translations.idiomatic: Yet court deliberation would have Your Majesty treat Xiaozong as father above while also treating Emperor Xian as father—this is the Han dynasty's error of dual successions.

sentences.zh: 本原既差，則愈議愈失。

translations.literal: Once the root principle is wrong, the more one deliberates the more one errs.
translations.idiomatic: Once the root principle is wrong, the more one deliberates, the further one strays.

sentences.zh: 臣之愚慮，則願陛下預防未然之失，毋重將來之悔而已。

translations.literal: Your servant's humble consideration is only that Your Majesty guard against errors not yet come to pass and not repeat regrets hereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's humble counsel is only that Your Majesty guard against errors not yet come to pass and not repeat regrets in the future.

sentences.zh: 始陛下尊昭聖皇太后為母，雖於禮未合，然宮闈之內亦既相安。

translations.literal: At first Your Majesty honored Empress Dowager Zhaosheng as mother; though not in accord with rites, within the inner palace all had nonetheless found peace.
translations.idiomatic: At first Your Majesty honored Empress Dowager Zhaosheng as mother; though the rites were not fully correct, peace had nonetheless settled within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 今一旦改稱，大非人情所堪。

translations.literal: To change the designation in a single day is more than human feeling can bear.
translations.idiomatic: To change the designation overnight is more than human feeling can bear.

sentences.zh: 願陛下以臣等建議之情，上啟皇太后，必中心悅預無疑貳之隙。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty, taking our memorial's intent, report upward to the empress dowager, so that at heart she will be pleased in advance and no doubt or division will arise.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty, taking the spirit of our memorial, report upward to the empress dowager, so that her heart will be at ease beforehand and no suspicion or rift will arise.

sentences.zh: 萬一未喻，亦得歸罪臣等，加賜誅斥，然後委曲申請，務得其歡心。

translations.literal: If by any chance she has not understood, blame may still be placed on us and we may be punished and dismissed; only then may you petition tactfully, striving to win her heartfelt approval.
translations.idiomatic: If by any chance she has not understood, blame may be placed on us and we punished and dismissed; only then may you petition tactfully and strive to win her heartfelt approval.

sentences.zh: 陛下朝夕所以承迎其意，慰釋其憂者，亦無所不用其極，庶名分正而嫌隙消，天下萬世無所非議，此臣愚慮者一也。

translations.literal: Everything Your Majesty does morning and evening to welcome her wishes and soothe her distress should be carried to the utmost, so that titles and stations may be set right and suspicion dissolved, and for ten thousand generations under Heaven there will be no dissent—this is the first point of your servant's humble consideration.
translations.idiomatic: In welcoming her wishes and soothing her distress morning and evening, Your Majesty should spare no effort, so that titles may be set right and suspicion dissolved, and for ten thousand generations under Heaven there will be no dissent—this is the first point of your servant's humble counsel.

sentences.zh: 昭聖之嫡嗣，武宗一人而已。

translations.literal: Of Zhaosheng's legitimate offspring, Wuzong alone exists.
translations.idiomatic: Of Zhaosheng's legitimate offspring, Wuzong alone remains.

sentences.zh: 武宗無嗣，莊肅皇后之屬望已矣。

translations.literal: Wuzong has no heir; Empress Zhuangsu's hopes are exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong has no heir; Empress Zhuangsu's hopes are spent.

sentences.zh: 臣謂陛下之事昭聖，禮秩雖極尊崇，然其勢日輕；

translations.literal: Your servant holds that in Your Majesty's dealings with Zhaosheng, though ritual rank is supremely elevated, yet her influence grows daily lighter;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that in Your Majesty's dealings with Zhaosheng, though ritual rank is supremely elevated, her influence grows daily lighter;

sentences.zh: 陛下之事聖母，尊稱雖或未至，然其勢日重。

translations.literal: In Your Majesty's dealings with the Holy Mother, though honored titles may not yet have been fully granted, yet her influence grows daily heavier.
translations.idiomatic: In Your Majesty's dealings with the Holy Mother, though honored titles may not yet have been fully granted, her influence grows daily heavier.

sentences.zh: 故今日廷臣惓惓以尊大統，母昭聖為請者，蓋預防陛下將來之失，而追報孝宗之職分也。

translations.literal: Therefore the court officials who earnestly appeal on Zhaosheng's behalf to uphold the great succession do so to guard against errors Your Majesty may yet commit and to fulfill filial duty toward Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the court officials who earnestly appeal on Zhaosheng's behalf to uphold the great succession do so to guard against errors Your Majesty may yet commit and to fulfill the duty owed Xiaozong.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗伏讀明詔，正統大義，不敢有違。

translations.literal: Your servant has humbly read the clear edicts and would not dare violate the great principle of legitimate succession.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has humbly read the clear edicts and dares not violate the great principle of legitimate succession.

sentences.zh: 知陛下尊昭聖，敬莊肅，此心可上質天地，下信士庶矣。

translations.literal: I know Your Majesty honors Zhaosheng and respects Zhuangsu—this sincerity can be offered up to Heaven and Earth and trusted by officials and commoners alike.
translations.idiomatic: I know Your Majesty honors Zhaosheng and respects Zhuangsu—a sincerity that can be offered up to Heaven and Earth and trusted by officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 但恐左右之人不達聖意，妄生疑間。

translations.literal: Yet I fear those at Your Majesty's side may not grasp the sage intent and will recklessly sow suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I fear those at Your Majesty's side may not grasp the imperial intent and will recklessly sow suspicion.

sentences.zh: 或以彌文小節，遂構兩宮之隙，此不可不早慮而預防之也。

translations.literal: Over trivial textual niceties they may forge a rift between the two palaces—this must be considered early and guarded against.
translations.idiomatic: Over trivial textual niceties they may forge a rift between the two palaces—this cannot go unconsidered and must be guarded against early.

sentences.zh: 願陛下以臣等建議之情，上啟聖母曰，昭聖皇太后實大統嫡宗，至尊無對，伏願聖母時自謙抑，示尊敬至意。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty take our memorial's intent and report upward to the Holy Mother, saying: 'Empress Dowager Zhaosheng is in truth the legitimate lineage of the great succession, supreme and without peer—I humbly pray the Holy Mother will at times humble herself and show utmost respect.'
