translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty take the spirit of our memorial and report upward to the Holy Mother, saying: 'Empress Dowager Zhaosheng is in truth the legitimate lineage of the great succession, supreme and without peer—I humbly pray the Holy Mother will at times humble herself and show the utmost respect.'

sentences.zh: 莊肅皇后母儀天下十六年，聖母接見之儀，不可輕忽，凡正旦、賀壽，聖母每致謙讓不敢受納之意。

translations.literal: Empress Zhuangsu was mother to the realm for sixteen years; the ceremonies of the Holy Mother's reception of her must not be slighted. At New Year's Day and birthday congratulations alike, the Holy Mother should each time express humility and unwillingness to receive what is offered.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhuangsu was mother to the realm for sixteen years; the ceremonies by which the Holy Mother receives her must not be slighted. At New Year's Day and birthday congratulations alike, the Holy Mother should each time express humility and unwillingness to accept what is offered.

sentences.zh: 俾宮闈大權一歸昭聖，而聖母若無與焉，則天下萬世稱頌懿德與天無極。

translations.literal: Thus let the great authority of the inner palace rest wholly with Zhaosheng, while the Holy Mother appears as if uninvolved—then for ten thousand generations under Heaven her admirable virtue will be praised as boundless as Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Let the great authority of the inner palace rest wholly with Zhaosheng, while the Holy Mother appears as if uninvolved—then for ten thousand generations under Heaven her admirable virtue will be praised as boundless as Heaven.

sentences.zh: 萬一聖母意猶未喻，亦得歸罪臣等，加賜誅斥，然後委曲申請，務得允從，庶宗統正而嫌隙消，天下萬世無所非議，此臣愚慮者二也。

translations.literal: If by any chance the Holy Mother has not yet understood, blame may still be placed on us and we may be punished and dismissed; only then may you petition tactfully and strive for her assent, so that the lineage may be set right and suspicion dissolved and for ten thousand generations under Heaven there will be no dissent—this is the second point of your servant's humble consideration."
translations.idiomatic: If by any chance the Holy Mother has not yet understood, blame may be placed on us and we punished and dismissed; only then may you petition tactfully and strive for her assent, so that the lineage may be set right, suspicion dissolved, and for ten thousand generations under Heaven there will be no dissent—this is the second point of your servant's humble counsel."

sentences.zh: 帝深嘉其忠義，趣令趨朝。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply praised his loyalty and righteousness and urgently ordered him to hurry to court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply praised his loyalty and righteousness and urgently ordered him to come to court at once.

sentences.zh: 明年擢少詹事兼侍講學士。

translations.literal: The following year he was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Lecturer-in-Waiting and Academician.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Lecturer-in-Waiting and Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 韜固辭。

translations.literal: Tao firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Tao firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 且請令六部長貳、翰林、給事、禦中俱調外任，練政體；

translations.literal: He also requested that vice ministers of the Six Ministries, Hanlin academicians, supervising secretaries, and Secretariat drafters all be rotated to outside posts to train in the substance of governance;
translations.idiomatic: He also requested that vice ministers of the Six Ministries, Hanlin academicians, supervising secretaries, and Secretariat drafters all be rotated to provincial posts to train in the substance of governance;

sentences.zh: 監司、守令政績卓異，即擢卿丞，有文學者擢翰林；

translations.literal: Outstanding grand coordinators and magistrates should immediately be promoted to vice ministers and assistants, and those with literary talent promoted to Hanlin;
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinators and magistrates with outstanding records should immediately be promoted to vice ministers and assistants, and those with literary talent promoted to Hanlin;

sentences.zh: 舉貢入仕皆得擢翰林，升部院，不宜困資格。

translations.literal: Men who entered service through recommendation and tribute should all be eligible for Hanlin appointment and advancement within ministries and courts—one should not confine them by seniority rules.
translations.idiomatic: Men who entered service through recommendation and tribute should all be eligible for Hanlin appointment and advancement within ministries and courts—they should not be trapped by seniority rules.

sentences.zh: 帝不允辭，趣令赴職。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit his resignation and urgently ordered him to take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused his resignation and urgently ordered him to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 下其奏於有司，悉格不用。

translations.literal: The memorial was referred to the appropriate offices; all proposals were rejected and not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the appropriate offices; all proposals were rejected.

sentences.zh: 六年，還朝，命直經筵日講。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he returned to court and was ordered to serve on daily exposition duty at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he returned to court and was ordered to serve on daily exposition duty at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 韜自以南音力辭日講，請撰《古今政要》及《詩書直解》以進。

translations.literal: Tao, citing his southern accent, vigorously declined daily exposition and requested to compile Essentials of Governance Past and Present and Direct Expositions of the Book of Poetry and Book of Documents for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: Tao, citing his southern accent, vigorously declined daily exposition and requested to compile Essentials of Governance Past and Present and Direct Expositions of the Book of Poetry and Book of Documents to present to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝褒許之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and approved the request.

sentences.zh: 其年九月遷詹事兼翰林學士，韜復固辭，言：「自楊榮、楊士奇、楊溥以及李東陽、楊廷和顓權植黨，籠翰林為屬官，中書為門吏，故翰林遷擢不由吏部，而中書至有進秩尚書者。

translations.literal: That ninth month he was transferred to Guardian of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Hanlin Academician. Tao again firmly declined, saying: "From Yang Rong, Yang Shiqi, and Yang Pu to Li Dongyang and Yang Tinghe, they monopolized power and planted factions, treating Hanlin as subordinate officials and the Secretariat as gate servants—thus Hanlin promotions no longer passed through the Ministry of Personnel, and Secretariat officials even rose to ministerial rank.
translations.idiomatic: That ninth month he was transferred to Guardian of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Hanlin Academician. Tao again firmly declined, saying: "From Yang Rong, Yang Shiqi, and Yang Pu to Li Dongyang and Yang Tinghe, they monopolized power and built factions, treating Hanlin as subordinate officials and the Secretariat as gate servants—so Hanlin promotions no longer passed through the Ministry of Personnel, and Secretariat officials even rose to ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗建議，謂翰林去留，盡屬吏部，庶不陰倚內閣為腹心，內閣亦不陰結翰林為羽翼。

translations.literal: Your servant once proposed that Hanlin appointments and dismissals should all belong to the Ministry of Personnel, so that neither would the Grand Secretariat secretly rely on Hanlin as its inner core, nor would the Grand Secretariat secretly bind Hanlin as its wings.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant once proposed that Hanlin appointments and dismissals should all belong to the Ministry of Personnel, so that the Grand Secretariat would not secretly rely on Hanlin as its inner core, nor secretly bind Hanlin as its wings.

sentences.zh: 且欲京官補外以均勞逸，議未即行，躬自蹈之，而又躐居學士徐縉上，何愧如之。」

translations.literal: Moreover, wishing capital officials to fill outside posts to balance labor and rest—the proposal was not immediately carried out, yet I myself trample on it, and moreover leap over Academician Xu Jin—what shame can compare to this?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I had wished capital officials to fill outside posts to balance labor and rest—the proposal was not immediately carried out, yet I myself violate it, and moreover leap over Academician Xu Jin—what shame can compare?"

sentences.zh: 帝優詔不允。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a gracious edict refusing his request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a gracious edict refusing his request.

sentences.zh: 明年四月進禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: The following April he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The following April he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 韜力辭，且舉康海、王九思、李夢陽、魏校、顏木、王廷陳、何瑭自代，帝不允。

translations.literal: Tao vigorously declined and recommended Kang Hai, Wang Jiusi, Li Mengyang, Wei Jiao, Yan Mu, Wang Tingchen, and He Tang to replace him; the emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Tao vigorously declined and recommended Kang Hai, Wang Jiusi, Li Mengyang, Wei Jiao, Yan Mu, Wang Tingchen, and He Tang in his stead; the emperor did not agree.

sentences.zh: 再辭，乃允之。

translations.literal: After declining again, the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: After he declined again, the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 六月，「大禮」成，超拜禮部尚書，掌詹事府事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, when the "Great Rites" were accomplished, he was extraordinarily promoted to Minister of Rites and put in charge of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, when the "Great Rites" were accomplished, he was extraordinarily promoted to Minister of Rites and put in charge of the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 韜因言翰林院修書遷官、日講蔭子、及巡撫子弟蔭武職之非，而以為己不能力挽，不可隨眾趨。

translations.literal: Tao thereupon spoke against the impropriety of Hanlin's promotion through book compilation, the hereditary privilege granted sons of daily lecturers, and the military hereditary appointments granted to grand coordinators' sons; he held that since he could not forcefully reverse these, he ought not follow the crowd in rushing forward.
translations.idiomatic: Tao thereupon spoke against the impropriety of Hanlin promotion through book compilation, hereditary privilege for sons of daily lecturers, and military hereditary appointments for grand coordinators' sons; since he could not forcefully reverse these, he held that he ought not follow the crowd in rushing forward.

sentences.zh: 且稱給事中陳洸冤，薦監生陳雲章才可用。

translations.literal: He also declared Supervising Secretary Chen Guang wronged and recommended Student Chen Yunzhang as a man of usable talent.
translations.idiomatic: He also declared Supervising Secretary Chen Guang wronged and recommended Student Chen Yunzhang as a man of usable talent.

sentences.zh: 帝優詔褒答，不允辭。

translations.literal: The emperor responded with a gracious edict of praise and did not permit his resignation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor responded with a gracious edict of praise and refused his resignation.

sentences.zh: 韜復奏曰：「今異議者謂陛下特欲尊崇皇考，遂以官爵餌其臣，臣等二三臣茍圖官爵，遂阿順陛下之意。

translations.literal: Tao submitted again, saying: "Today those who dissent say Your Majesty merely wishes to honor your imperial father and so bait his officials with rank and stipends—that we few officials grasp at rank and stipends and therefore flatter Your Majesty's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Tao submitted again, saying: "Today those who dissent say Your Majesty merely wishes to honor your imperial father and bait his officials with rank and stipends—that we few officials grasp at rank and stipends and therefore flatter Your Majesty's intent.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗自慨，若得禮定，決不受官，俾天下萬世知議禮者非利官也。

translations.literal: Your servant once vowed in private that if the rites were settled, I would certainly not accept office, so that for ten thousand generations under Heaven all would know that those who debated the rites sought not profit in office.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant once vowed in private that if the rites were settled, I would accept no office, so that for ten thousand generations under Heaven all would know that those who debated the rites sought not profit in office.

sentences.zh: 茍疑議禮者為利官，則所議雖是，彼猶以為非，何以塞天下口？」

translations.literal: If one suspects that those who debated the rites sought profit in office, then even if what was debated was right, they will still deem it wrong—how can one stop the mouths of the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: If one suspects that those who debated the rites sought profit in office, then even if what was debated was right, they will still deem it wrong—how can one silence the realm?"

sentences.zh: 因固辭不拜，帝猶不允。

translations.literal: Thereupon he firmly declined to accept the appointment; the emperor still did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he firmly declined to accept the appointment; the emperor still refused.

sentences.zh: 三辭，乃允之。

translations.literal: After declining three times, the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: After he declined three times, the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 韜先後薦王守仁、王瓊諸人，帝皆納用。

translations.literal: Tao successively recommended Wang Shouren, Wang Qiong, and others; the emperor adopted them all.
translations.idiomatic: Tao successively recommended Wang Shouren, Wang Qiong, and others; the emperor adopted them all.

sentences.zh: 嘗因災異陳時弊十余事，多議行。

translations.literal: On one occasion, citing calamities and portents, he presented more than ten present abuses; most were deliberated and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion, citing calamities and portents, he presented more than ten abuses of the age; most were deliberated and carried out.

sentences.zh: 張璁、桂萼之罷政也，韜謂言官陸粲等受楊一清指使，兩疏力攻一清，奪其職，而璁、萼召還。

translations.literal: When Zhang Cong and Gui E were removed from government, Tao held that remonstrating officials such as Lu Can acted at Yang Yiqing's direction; with two memorials he vigorously attacked Yiqing, stripped him of his post, and Cong and E were recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Cong and Gui E were removed from government, Tao held that remonstrating officials such as Lu Can acted at Yang Yiqing's direction; with two memorials he vigorously attacked Yiqing, stripped him of his post, and Cong and E were recalled.

sentences.zh: 帝從夏言議，將分祀天地，建二郊，韜極言其非。

translations.literal: The emperor followed Xia Yan's proposal to sacrifice separately to Heaven and Earth and establish twin suburban altars; Tao spoke out strongly against it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed Xia Yan's proposal to sacrifice separately to Heaven and Earth and establish twin suburban altars; Tao spoke out strongly against it.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，責韜罔上自恣。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and rebuked Tao for deceiving his sovereign and acting willfully.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and rebuked Tao for deceiving his sovereign and acting willfully.

sentences.zh: 言亦疏辨，力詆韜。

translations.literal: Yan also submitted a memorial in defense and vigorously denounced Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Yan also submitted a memorial in his own defense and vigorously denounced Tao.

sentences.zh: 韜素護前自遂，見帝怒，不敢辨，乃遺言書，痛詆之，復錄其書送法司。

translations.literal: Tao, who habitually obstinately defended his prior positions, seeing the emperor's anger, did not dare rebut; instead he sent a letter to Yan, bitterly denouncing him, and also copied the letter and sent it to the judicial offices.
translations.idiomatic: Tao, who habitually obstinately defended his prior positions, seeing the emperor's anger, did not dare rebut; instead he sent Yan a letter bitterly denouncing him, and also copied the letter and sent it to the judicial offices.

sentences.zh: 言怒，疏陳其狀，且劾韜無君七罪，並以其書進呈。

translations.literal: Yan was enraged; he submitted a memorial detailing the circumstances and impeached Tao on seven counts of disloyalty to the ruler, also presenting Tao's letter to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was enraged; he submitted a memorial detailing the circumstances and impeached Tao on seven counts of disloyalty to the ruler, also presenting Tao's letter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，責韜謗訕君上，醜正懷邪，遂下都察院獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, rebuked Tao for slandering his sovereign and hating the upright while harboring the corrupt, and had him imprisoned in the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angered, rebuked Tao for slandering his sovereign and hating the upright while harboring the corrupt, and had him imprisoned in the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 韜從獄中上書祈哀，璁亦再申救，帝皆不納。

translations.literal: Tao from prison submitted a memorial pleading for mercy; Cong also twice interceded on his behalf; the emperor accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: From prison Tao submitted a memorial pleading for mercy; Cong also twice interceded on his behalf; the emperor accepted neither.

sentences.zh: 南京御史鄧文憲言，宜察韜心，容其戇，且天地分祀是置父母異處，郊外親蠶是廢內外防閑。

translations.literal: Nanjing Censor Deng Wenxian said Tao's intent should be examined, his bluntness indulged, and furthermore that separate sacrifices to Heaven and Earth amounted to placing father and mother in different places, while the empress's silkworm rite in the suburbs abolished the inner-outer barrier.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing Censor Deng Wenxian said Tao's intent should be examined and his bluntness indulged, and furthermore that separate sacrifices to Heaven and Earth amounted to placing father and mother in different places, while the empress's silkworm rite in the suburbs abolished the inner-outer barrier.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，謫之邊方。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and banished him to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and banished him to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 韜系獄逾月，帝終念其議禮功，令輸贖還職。

translations.literal: Tao remained imprisoned for more than a month; the emperor at last remembered his merit in the rites debate and ordered him to pay a fine and return to office.
translations.idiomatic: Tao remained imprisoned for more than a month; the emperor at last remembered his merit in the rites debate and ordered him to pay a fine and return to office.

sentences.zh: 尋以母喪歸。

translations.literal: Soon after he returned home upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he returned home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 廣東僉事龔大稔訐韜及方獻夫居鄉不法事，大稔反被逮削籍。

translations.literal: Guangdong Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Gong Danan impeached Tao and Fang Xianfu for unlawful conduct while living in their home districts; Danan himself was instead arrested and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Gong Danan impeached Tao and Fang Xianfu for unlawful conduct in their home districts; Danan himself was instead arrested and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 十二年，韜起歷吏部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Tao was recalled and served successively as Left and Right Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Tao was recalled and served successively as Left and Right Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時部事多主於尚書，兩侍郎率不預。

translations.literal: At the time most ministry affairs were decided by the minister; the two vice ministers generally did not participate.
translations.idiomatic: At the time most ministry affairs were decided by the minister alone; the two vice ministers generally did not participate.

sentences.zh: 韜爭於尚書汪鋐，侍郎始獲參部事。

translations.literal: Tao contended with Minister Wang Gong until vice ministers at last gained participation in ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tao contended with Minister Wang Gong until the vice ministers at last gained participation in ministry affairs.

sentences.zh: 韜素剛愎，屢與鋐爭，鋐等亦嚴憚之。

translations.literal: Tao was by nature stubborn and obstinate, repeatedly clashing with Gong; Gong and the others also deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was by nature stubborn and obstinate, repeatedly clashing with Gong; Gong and the others also deeply feared him.

sentences.zh: 既而鋐罷，帝久不置尚書，以韜掌部事。

translations.literal: Later Gong was dismissed; the emperor for a long time did not appoint a minister and had Tao manage ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later Gong was dismissed; the emperor for a long time appointed no minister and had Tao manage ministry affairs.

sentences.zh: 閣臣李時傳旨，用鴻臚卿王道中為順天府丞。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Li Shi transmitted an edict appointing Ceremonial Reception Director Wang Daozhong as assistant magistrate of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Li Shi transmitted an edict appointing Ceremonial Reception Director Wang Daozhong as assistant magistrate of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 韜言：「輔臣承天語無可疑，然臣等猶當奏請，用杜矯偽。」

translations.literal: Tao said: "The assisting minister bears the heavenly words—there can be no doubt; yet we ought still to memorialize for approval, to guard against forgery."
translations.idiomatic: Tao said: "The assisting minister bears the heavenly words—there can be no doubt; yet we ought still to memorialize for approval, to guard against forgery."

sentences.zh: 因守故事，列道中及應天府丞郭登庸二人名上。

translations.literal: Accordingly, following precedent, he submitted the names of both Daozhong and Assistant Magistrate of Yingtian Prefecture Guo Dengyong.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, following precedent, he submitted the names of both Daozhong and Assistant Magistrate of Yingtian Prefecture Guo Dengyong.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其守法，乃用登庸，而改道中大理少卿。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him for observing the law and then appointed Dengyong, while transferring Daozhong to Vice Director of Penalties in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him for observing the law and then appointed Dengyong, while transferring Daozhong to Vice Director of Penalties in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 久之，出韜為南京禮部尚書。

translations.literal: After some time Tao was transferred out as Minister of Rites in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Tao was transferred out as Minister of Rites in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 順天府尹劉淑相坐所親贓私被鞫，疑禮部尚書夏言姻通判費完陷之，訐言請屬事。

translations.literal: Shuntian Prefecture Magistrate Liu Shuxiang, because a close associate was imprisoned for graft, suspected Minister of Rites Xia Yan's in-law Assistant Prefect Fei Wan of framing him and impeached Yan for soliciting favors.
translations.idiomatic: Shuntian Prefecture Magistrate Liu Shuxiang, because a close associate was imprisoned for graft, suspected that Minister of Rites Xia Yan's in-law Assistant Prefect Fei Wan had framed him and impeached Yan for soliciting favors.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下淑相詔獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and imprisoned Shuxiang in the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and imprisoned Shuxiang in the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 淑相與韜善，言亦疑韜主之，遂訐韜扈蹕謁陵，遠遊銀山寺大不敬。

translations.literal: Shuxiang was on good terms with Tao; Yan also suspected Tao had instigated this and therefore impeached Tao for escorting the emperor to visit the imperial tombs yet roaming far to Yingshan Temple—a grave lack of reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Shuxiang was on good terms with Tao; Yan also suspected Tao had instigated this and therefore impeached Tao for escorting the emperor to visit the imperial tombs yet roaming far to Yingshan Temple—a grave lack of reverence.

sentences.zh: 韜自訴，因論言：「請謚故少師費宏為文憲，不敘宏累被劾狀，按律，增減緊關情節者斬。

translations.literal: Tao pleaded in his own defense and by the same token argued against Yan: "In requesting the posthumous title Literary Exemplar for the late Junior Preceptor Fei Hong, you did not recount Hong's repeated impeachments—by law, altering crucial circumstances merits decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Tao pleaded in his own defense and by the same token argued against Yan: "In requesting the posthumous title Literary Exemplar for the late Junior Preceptor Fei Hong, you did not recount Hong's repeated impeachments—by law, altering crucial circumstances merits decapitation.

sentences.zh: 且『憲』乃純皇帝廟號，人臣安得用？」

translations.literal: Moreover, 'Exemplar' is the temple name of Emperor Chun—how dare a subject use it?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, 'Exemplar' is the temple name of Emperor Chun—how dare a subject use it?"

sentences.zh: 會南京給事中曾鈞騎馬，不避尚書劉龍、潘珍轎，龍與鈞互訐奏。

translations.literal: At the same time Nanjing Supervising Secretary Zeng Jun rode on horseback and did not yield to the litters of Ministers Liu Long and Pan Zhen; Long and Jun mutually impeached each other in memorials.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Nanjing Supervising Secretary Zeng Jun rode on horseback and did not yield to the litters of Ministers Liu Long and Pan Zhen; Long and Jun mutually impeached each other in memorials.

sentences.zh: 韜劾鈞，且請禁小臣乘轎。

translations.literal: Tao impeached Jun and also requested a ban on minor officials riding in litters.
translations.idiomatic: Tao impeached Jun and also requested a ban on minor officials riding in litters.

sentences.zh: 給事中李充濁、曹邁等交章，言近侍之臣不當避道，雜舉公會宴次得與尚書同列以證，語頗侵韜。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Li Chongzhuo, Cao Mai, and others submitted memorials in succession, arguing that officials close to the throne ought not yield the road, citing mixed examples of sharing rank with ministers at public banquets as proof—language that somewhat impugned Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Li Chongzhuo, Cao Mai, and others submitted memorials in succession, arguing that officials close to the throne ought not yield the road, citing mixed examples of sharing rank with ministers at public banquets as proof—language that somewhat impugned Tao.

sentences.zh: 韜疑充濁倚言為內主，訐充濁為奸黨，復摭言他事。

translations.literal: Tao suspected Chongzhuo relied on Yan as his patron within and impeached Chongzhuo as part of a corrupt faction, also dredging up other matters concerning Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Tao suspected Chongzhuo relied on Yan as his patron within and impeached Chongzhuo as part of a corrupt faction, also dredging up other matters concerning Yan.

sentences.zh: 言益怒，奏韜大罪十余事。

translations.literal: Yan grew still angrier and memorialized more than ten grave crimes of Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Yan grew still angrier and memorialized more than ten grave crimes of Tao.

sentences.zh: 且言彭時、宋濂皆於正德間謚文憲，不避廟號，韜陋不知故事。

translations.literal: He also said that Peng Shi and Song Lian both received the posthumous title Literary Exemplar in the Zhengde era without avoiding the temple name—Tao was crude and ignorant of precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that Peng Shi and Song Lian both received the posthumous title Literary Exemplar in the Zhengde era without avoiding the temple name—Tao was crude and ignorant of precedent.

sentences.zh: 帝方不直韜，淑相復從獄中摭言他事，帝益怒，考訊之。

translations.literal: The emperor was just then not upright toward Tao; Shuxiang again from within prison picked out other matters concerning Yan; the emperor increased in anger and examined and interrogated him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was already inclined against Tao; Shuxiang again dredged up from prison other charges against Yan, and the emperor, growing still angrier, had him interrogated under torture.

sentences.zh: 辭服韜主使，乃斥淑相為民，降韜俸一級。

translations.literal: In his words he submitted that Tao had been the master who sent him; thereupon Shuxiang was expelled as a commoner, and Tao's salary was reduced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: In his confession he acknowledged Tao had instigated him; Shuxiang was demoted to commoner status, and Tao's salary was cut one rank.

sentences.zh: 當議乘轎時，言被劾不預，都御史王廷相會禮部侍郎黃宗明、張璧請禁飭小臣如韜奏，而南京諸給事、御史自如。

translations.literal: When the riding-in-litters matter was debated, Yan was impeached and did not participate; Censor-in-Chief Wang Tingsxiang joined Vice Ministers of Rites Huang Zongming and Zhang Bi in requesting prohibition and restraint of minor officials as Tao had memorialized, yet the various supervising secretaries and censors at Nanjing were as before.
translations.idiomatic: While the litter ban was under debate, Yan was under impeachment and took no part; Censor-in-Chief Wang Tingsxiang, together with Vice Ministers of Rites Huang Zongming and Zhang Bi, asked that minor officials be restrained as Tao had proposed—but the Nanjing supervising secretaries and censors went on as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 韜以為言，帝復申飭，眾情滋不悅。

translations.literal: Tao took this as grounds for complaint; the emperor again reiterated the restraint, and the multitude's sentiment grew ever more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Tao complained of this; the emperor reiterated the restriction, and public sentiment turned ever more sour.

sentences.zh: 曹邁及同官尹相等遂與韜忿爭。

translations.literal: Cao Mai and his colleague Yin Xiang and others thereupon had an angry dispute with Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Mai, his colleague Yin Xiang, and others then quarreled furiously with Tao.

sentences.zh: 相劾韜遷南部怨望；

translations.literal: Xiang impeached Tao for resentment and complaint over transfer to the southern capital;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang impeached Tao for nursing resentment over his transfer to the southern capital;

sentences.zh: 擅取海子魚，與鄉人群飲郊壇松下；

translations.literal: for taking fish from the imperial lake without authorization and drinking in groups with villagers under the pines at the suburban altar;
translations.idiomatic: for poaching fish from the imperial lake and carousing with villagers beneath the pines at the suburban altar;

sentences.zh: 侍郎袁宗儒期喪不當進表，逼使行。

translations.literal: for forcing Vice Minister Yuan Zongru, who was in the mourning period and ought not to submit a memorial, to do so.
translations.idiomatic: and for forcing Vice Minister Yuan Zongru, still in mourning and forbidden to submit memorials, to do so anyway.

sentences.zh: 韜上疏自理。

translations.literal: Tao submitted a memorial to explain himself.
translations.idiomatic: Tao submitted a memorial in self-defense.

sentences.zh: 下廷議。

translations.literal: It was sent down for court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to court deliberation.

sentences.zh: 帝為停韜俸四月，相等亦停二月。

translations.literal: The emperor on Tao's behalf suspended salary four months; Xiang and the others also had salary suspended two months.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspended Tao's salary for four months and likewise suspended Xiang and his colleagues for two months.

sentences.zh: 韜既與言交惡，及言柄用，韜每欲因事陷之。

translations.literal: Tao had already been on bad terms with Yan in mutual enmity; once Yan held power in use, Tao every time wished to trap him by some affair.
translations.idiomatic: Tao and Yan were already bitter enemies; once Yan came to power, Tao constantly sought some pretext to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 上言：「頃吏部選劉文光等為給事中，尋忽報罷，人皆曰閣臣抑之。

translations.literal: He memorialized upward, saying: "Recently the Ministry of Personnel selected Liu Wenguang and others as supervising secretaries; soon word suddenly came they were dismissed—all say the grand secretaries suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Recently the Ministry of Personnel selected Liu Wenguang and others as supervising secretaries, but soon they were reported dismissed—everyone says the grand secretaries blocked the appointments.

sentences.zh: 給事中李鶴鳴考察謫官，尋復故，人皆曰賄得。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Li Heming was evaluated and demoted; soon he was restored to his former post—all say he obtained it by bribe.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Li Heming was evaluated, demoted, then soon restored—everyone says he bought his way back.

sentences.zh: 宜諭吏部毋受當事頤指，使天下知威福出朝廷，而大臣有李林甫、秦檜者，不得播弄於左右。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to instruct the Ministry of Personnel not to accept the chin-and-finger directions of those in power, so that all under Heaven may know authority and favor issue from the court, and grand ministers like Li Linfu and Qin Hui may not manipulate affairs at the left and right."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel should be told not to take dictation from those in power, so that all under Heaven may know authority and favor come from the throne—and ministers like Li Linfu and Qin Hui may not pull strings at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 其意為言發也。

translations.literal: His intent was to attack Yan in launching it.
translations.idiomatic: His aim was plainly to strike at Yan.

sentences.zh: 於是鶴鳴上疏自白，並摭韜居鄉不法諸事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Heming submitted a memorial to clear himself, and also picked out Tao's unlawful conduct in his home district on various matters.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Heming memorialized to clear himself and dredged up Tao's misdeeds at home.

sentences.zh: 帝兩置之。

translations.literal: The emperor set both aside.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored both memorials.

sentences.zh: 無何，韜劾南京御史龔湜、郭本。

translations.literal: Before long, Tao impeached Nanjing censors Gong Shi and Guo Ben.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Tao impeached the Nanjing censors Gong Shi and Guo Ben.

sentences.zh: 湜等自辨，亦劾韜。

translations.literal: Shi and the others defended themselves and also impeached Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Shi and the others defended themselves and impeached Tao in turn.

sentences.zh: 帝並置不問。

translations.literal: The emperor set all aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed all of it without investigation.

sentences.zh: 十八年簡補宮僚，命韜以太子少保、禮部尚書協掌詹事府事。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year palace adjuncts were selected and replenished; Tao was ordered to serve as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Rites to assist in directing the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, when palace staff were chosen to fill vacancies, Tao was appointed Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Rites to assist in directing the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 疏辭加秩，且詆大臣受祿不讓，晉秩不辭，或有狐鼠鉆結，陰固寵權，怨氣召災。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial declining the added rank and also disparaged grand ministers who accepted emoluments without declining and accepted promotions without refusal—perhaps foxes and rats bore holes and linked up, secretly consolidating favor and power, and resentful qi summoned calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to decline the added rank and disparaged grand ministers who took salary without refusing it and accepted promotion without demur—perhaps cronies schemed in the dark to hold favor and power, and accumulated resentment summoned disaster.

sentences.zh: 實有所自。

translations.literal: It truly had a source of its own.
translations.idiomatic: He clearly had someone particular in mind.

sentences.zh: 其意亦為言發。

translations.literal: His intent was again to attack Yan in launching it.
translations.idiomatic: Again his barbs were aimed at Yan.

sentences.zh: 既屢擊言不勝，最後見郭勛與言有隙，乃陰比勛，與共齮龁言。

translations.literal: Having repeatedly attacked Yan without victory, at last seeing Guo Xun at odds with Yan, he secretly aligned with Xun and jointly gnawed at Yan.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated attacks on Yan failed, he saw Guo Xun was at odds with Yan and secretly joined him to undermine Yan together.

sentences.zh: 時中外訛言帝復南幸，韜因顯頌勛，言：「六飛南狩時，臣下多納賄不法。

translations.literal: At the time rumor within and without said the emperor would again tour south favorably; Tao therefore openly praised Xun, saying: "When the six-horse carriage went south on hunt-tour, many officials below accepted bribes unlawfully.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread at court and beyond that the emperor would tour south again; Tao openly praised Xun, saying: "When the imperial procession toured south, many officials accepted bribes and broke the law.

sentences.zh: 文官惟袁宗儒，武官惟郭勛不受饋。

translations.literal: Among civil officials only Yuan Zongru; among military officials only Guo Xun did not accept gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Of the civil officials, only Yuan Zongru; of the military officials, only Guo Xun refused bribes.

sentences.zh: 今訛言復播，宜有以禁戢之。」

translations.literal: Now the rumor spreads again—it is fitting that there be something to prohibit and restrain it."
translations.idiomatic: Now the rumor spreads again—something should be done to suppress it.

sentences.zh: 帝既下詔安群情，乃詰韜曰：「朕昨南巡，卿不在行，受賄事得自何人？

translations.literal: The emperor, having already issued an edict to settle the multitude's sentiment, then interrogated Tao, saying: "I yesterday toured south; you were not in the entourage—on the matter of accepting bribes, from whom did this come?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, having issued an edict to calm public anxiety, then pressed Tao: "On my southern tour you were not in the entourage—who told you officials took bribes?

sentences.zh: 據實以奏。」

translations.literal: Report according to the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Report the facts.

sentences.zh: 韜對，請問諸郭勛。

translations.literal: Tao replied, requesting to question Guo Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Tao replied by asking that Guo Xun be questioned.

sentences.zh: 帝責其支詞，務令指實。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked his evasive words and insisted he point to concrete facts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked his evasiveness and demanded concrete names.

sentences.zh: 韜窘，乃言：「扈從諸臣無不受饋遺、折取夫隸直者，第問之夏言，令自述。

translations.literal: Tao, embarrassed, then said: "Among the officials escorting the emperor none failed to accept gifts or deduct corvée fees from the commoners—merely question Xia Yan and have him describe it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Tao said: "Every official in the imperial entourage accepted gifts or skimmed corvée fees from the people—just question Xia Yan and have him confess.

sentences.zh: 至各官取賄實跡，勛具悉始末，當不欺。

translations.literal: As for each official's concrete traces of accepting bribes, Xun knows the full beginning and end and will not deceive.
translations.idiomatic: As for the full record of who took what, Xun knows every detail and will not lie.

sentences.zh: 如必欲臣言，請假臣風憲職，循途按之，當備列以奏。」

translations.literal: If you must have this minister speak, please lend this minister censorial authority and have me investigate along the route—I shall fully enumerate and report."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty insists I speak, grant me censorial authority to investigate along the route—I will report everything I find.

sentences.zh: 章下所司。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 韜懼不當帝旨，尋赴京，列所遇進鮮船內臣貪橫狀，帝亦不問。

translations.literal: Tao feared he had missed the emperor's intent; soon he went to the capital and listed instances of greedy and overbearing eunuchs on tribute-ship routes he had encountered—the emperor likewise did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he had displeased the emperor, Tao soon went to the capital and listed cases of greedy, overbearing eunuchs on tribute boats he had met—but the emperor took no notice.

sentences.zh: 明年十月卒於官，年五十有四。

translations.literal: The next year in the tenth month he died in office, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: The following tenth month he died in office, aged fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚文敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Literary Keenness.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Literary Keenness.

sentences.zh: 韜學博才高，量褊隘，所至與人競。

translations.literal: Tao's learning was broad and his talent high; his measure was narrow and cramped—wherever he went he contended with people.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was learned and brilliant, but petty and narrow—wherever he went he picked fights.

sentences.zh: 帝頗心厭之，故不大用。

translations.literal: The emperor in heart somewhat grew weary of him; therefore he was not greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew weary of him at heart and never fully trusted him with power.

sentences.zh: 先後多所建白，亦頗涉國家大計。

translations.literal: First and last he memorialized on many matters and also considerably touched on great state policy.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted many proposals over the years, several touching matters of broad national concern.

sentences.zh: 且嘗薦「大禮」大獄得罪諸臣，及廢籍李夢陽、康海等。

translations.literal: And he once recommended officials condemned in the Great Rites and the great prosecutions, as well as those struck from the rolls like Li Mengyang and Kang Hai.
translations.idiomatic: He also once recommended officials ruined in the Great Rites prosecutions, and disgraced writers such as Li Mengyang and Kang Hai.

sentences.zh: 在南都，禁喪家宴飲，絕婦女入寺觀，罪娼戶市良人女，毀淫祠，建社學，散僧尼，表忠節。

translations.literal: In the southern capital he banned banquet drinking in mourning households, cut off women entering temples and monasteries, punished brothel households for buying commoners' daughters, destroyed illicit shrines, established community schools, dispersed monks and nuns, and honored loyalty and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanjing he banned feasting in houses of mourning, barred women from temples, punished brothels that bought freeborn girls, tore down illicit shrines, founded community schools, dispersed monks and nuns, and honored the loyal and steadfast.

sentences.zh: 既去，士民思之。

translations.literal: After he left, scholars and commoners missed him.
translations.idiomatic: After he left office, gentry and commoners alike missed him.

sentences.zh: 始與璁、萼結，既而比郭勛。

translations.literal: At first he allied with Cong and E; afterward he compared himself to Guo Xun.
translations.idiomatic: At first he joined Zhang Cong and Gui E; later he cast his lot with Guo Xun.

sentences.zh: 舉進士出毛澄門下，素執弟子禮，議禮不合，遂不復稱為座主。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination as a disciple of Mao Cheng and habitually observed disciples' rites toward him; when their debate on the rites disagreed, he never again called Cheng his patron.
translations.idiomatic: He had passed the jinshi under Mao Cheng and once observed full disciples' rites toward him; when they split over the rites debate, he never again called Cheng his patron.

sentences.zh: 及總裁己丑會試，亦遂不以唐順之等為門生。

translations.literal: When he served as chief examiner of the jichou metropolitan examination, he likewise no longer regarded Tang Shunzhi and others as his disciples.
translations.idiomatic: When he presided over the jichou metropolitan examination, he likewise refused to claim Tang Shunzhi and others as his disciples.

sentences.zh: 其議禮時，詆司馬光。

translations.literal: When debating the rites he disparaged Sima Guang.
translations.idiomatic: In the rites debate he attacked Sima Guang.

sentences.zh: 後議薛瑄從祀，至追論光不可祀孔廟。

translations.literal: Later, when Xue Xuan's enshrinement was debated, he went so far as to revisit the argument that Guang ought not be enshrined in the Confucian temple.
translations.idiomatic: Later, during debate over enshrining Xue Xuan, he revived his argument that Guang should be removed from the Confucian temple.

sentences.zh: 其不顧公論如此。

translations.literal: In disregarding public opinion he was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his contempt for public opinion.

sentences.zh: 子與瑕，舉進士。

translations.literal: His son Yuxia passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuxia passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 授慈溪知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Cixi.

sentences.zh: 鄢懋卿巡鹽行部，與瑕不禮，為所劾罷。

translations.literal: When Yan Maoqing toured the salt circuit and traveled through his department, Yuxia did not show him courtesy and was impeached and dismissed by him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Maoqing inspected the salt administration and passed through his jurisdiction, Yuxia withheld courtesy and was impeached out of office by him.

sentences.zh: 起知鄞縣，終廣西僉事。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as magistrate of Yin county and finally ended as Vice Commissioner in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as magistrate of Yin county and ended his career as Vice Commissioner in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 熊浹，字悅之，南昌人。

translations.literal: Xiong Jia, styled Yuezhi, was a native of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Jia, styled Yuezhi, was a native of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 正德九年進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhengde he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the ninth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 授禮科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a supervising secretary in the Rites Section.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠將為變，浹與同邑御史熊蘭草奏，授御史蕭淮上之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Ning Zhu Chenhao was about to rebel, Jia together with his townsman Censor Xiong Lan drafted a memorial and entrusted it to Censor Xiao Huai to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Ning Zhu Chenhao was preparing to rebel, Jia and his fellow townsman, Censor Xiong Lan, drafted a memorial and had Censor Xiao Huai submit it.

sentences.zh: 濠倉卒舉事，卒敗，本兩人早發之力。

translations.literal: When Chenhao rashly rose in revolt he was swiftly defeated—it was originally owed to the two men's early exposure.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao rose in haste and was quickly crushed—largely because these two men had exposed the plot early.

sentences.zh: 出核松潘邊餉。

translations.literal: He went out to audit border provisions at Songpan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to audit border provisions at Songpan.

sentences.zh: 副總兵張傑倚江彬勢，贓累巨萬，誘殺熟番上功啟邊釁，箠死千戶以下至五百人。

translations.literal: Deputy Commander-in-Chief Zhang Jie relied on Jiang Bin's power; his accumulated corruption ran to tens of thousands, he lured the killing of settled tribesmen to claim merit and provoke border trouble, and beat more than five hundred men from company commanders downward to death.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Commander Zhang Jie, backed by Jiang Bin, amassed corruption worth tens of thousands; he provoked killings among settled tribes to claim merit and stir border trouble, and had more than five hundred officers from company commanders down beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 又嘗率家眾遮擊副使胡澧。

translations.literal: He also once led his household retainers to intercept and attack Vice Commissioner Hu Li.
translations.idiomatic: He also once led his household retainers to ambush and attack Vice Commissioner Hu Li.

sentences.zh: 撫、按莫敢言。

translations.literal: The grand coordinator and regional inspector dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: The grand coordinator and regional inspector dared not report him.

sentences.zh: 浹至，盡發其狀，傑遂褫職。

translations.literal: When Jia arrived he fully exposed Jie's conduct and Jie was thereupon stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia arrived he exposed Jie's crimes in full, and Jie was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 世宗踐阼，廷議追崇禮未定。

translations.literal: When the Shizong emperor ascended the throne, court debate over posthumous honors for the rites remained unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, court debate over the rites of imperial mourning remained unsettled.

sentences.zh: 浹馳疏言：「陛下起自藩服，入登大寶，倘必執為後之說，考孝宗而母慈壽，則興獻母妃當降稱伯叔父母矣。

translations.literal: Jia urgently submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty rose from a princely establishment and entered to ascend the great treasure—if you insist on the theory of being made another's heir, honoring Xiaozong while taking Empress Cishou as mother, then the Prince of Xing's consort would have to be demoted to the title of paternal uncle's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Jia urgently memorialized: "Your Majesty rose from a princely fief to the throne—if you insist on the theory of adoption, honoring Emperor Xiaozong and taking Empress Cishou as mother, then the Prince of Xing's consort would be reduced to the rank of an uncle's wife.

sentences.zh: 不知陛下承歡內庭時，將仍舊稱乎，抑改而從今稱乎？

translations.literal: I do not know when Your Majesty was paying court in the inner palace—would you still have used the old titles, or changed to follow today's titles?
translations.idiomatic: When you paid court within the palace, would you have kept the old forms of address, or changed to the new ones?

sentences.zh: 若仍舊稱，而不得尊之為後，則於慈壽徒有為後之虛文，於母妃則又缺尊崇之大典，無一而可也。

translations.literal: If you still used the old titles yet could not honor her as heir, then toward Cishou you would have only the empty form of being an heir, while toward the Prince's consort you would again lack the great ceremony of highest honor—nothing would do.
translations.idiomatic: If you kept the old titles yet could not honor her as heir, Empress Cishou would receive only empty ceremony while your own mother would lack full honor—neither course would suffice.

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂興獻王尊以帝號，別建一廟，以示不敢上躋於列聖。

translations.literal: Your humble servant considers that the Prince of Xing should be honored with an imperial title and a separate temple built, to show reluctance to ascend above the successive sage emperors.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that the Prince of Xing be honored with an imperial title and a separate temple, showing that you dare not rank him above the ancestral emperors.

sentences.zh: 母妃則尊為皇太后，而少殺其徽稱，以示不敢上同於慈壽。

translations.literal: The consort should be honored as Empress Dowager, with her honorific title slightly reduced, to show reluctance to rank equal with Cishou.
translations.idiomatic: His consort should be honored as Empress Dowager, with a slightly lesser title, showing that you dare not rank her equal to Empress Cishou.

sentences.zh: 此於大統固無所妨，而天性之恩亦得以兼盡。」

translations.literal: This in no way impedes the great succession, yet the affection of natural feeling may also be fully fulfilled."
translations.idiomatic: This would not harm the imperial succession, yet would let natural filial affection be fully expressed.

sentences.zh: 疏至，會興王及妃已稱為帝後，下之禮官。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, it happened that the Prince of Xing and his consort had already been titled emperor and empress—it was sent down to the rites officials.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the Prince of Xing and his consort had already been titled emperor and empress; it was referred to the rites officials.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，由右給事中出為河南參議。

translations.literal: In the early Jiajing era he went out from Right Supervising Secretary to serve as Vice Commissioner in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In early Jiajing he left his post as Right Supervising Secretary to become Vice Commissioner in Henan.

sentences.zh: 外艱歸。

translations.literal: He returned on account of mourning for a parent.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to observe mourning for a parent.

sentences.zh: 六年，服闋，召修《明倫大典》。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when mourning ended, he was summoned to compile the Great Canon of Human Relations.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when mourning ended, he was summoned to compile the Great Canon of Human Relations.

sentences.zh: 超擢右僉都御史，協理院事。

translations.literal: He was specially promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to assist in directing court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to assist in directing the censorate.

sentences.zh: 明年四月遷大理寺卿，俄遷右副都御史。

translations.literal: The next year in the fourth month he was transferred to Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review; soon he was transferred to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The following fourth month he became Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review; soon after he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 《大典》成，轉左。

translations.literal: When the Great Canon was completed, he was transferred to the left.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Canon was completed, he was transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 八年二月遂擢右都御史，掌院事。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year he was then promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and directed court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and put in charge of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 京師民張福訴裏人張柱殺其母，東廠以聞，刑部坐柱死。

translations.literal: A commoner of the capital named Zhang Fu accused his neighbor Zhang Zhu of killing his mother; the Eastern Depot reported it and the Ministry of Punishments sentenced Zhu to death.
translations.idiomatic: A Beijing commoner named Zhang Fu accused his neighbor Zhang Zhu of killing his mother; the Eastern Depot reported it, and the Ministry of Punishments sentenced Zhu to death.

sentences.zh: 不服，福姊亦泣訴官，謂母福自殺之，其鄰人之詞亦然。

translations.literal: He would not submit; Fu's elder sister also wept and appealed to officials, saying their mother had been killed by Fu himself, and the neighbors' testimony likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu would not accept the verdict; Fu's elder sister wept before the magistrate, saying Fu had killed their mother himself, and the neighbors said the same.

sentences.zh: 詔郎中魏應召覆按，改坐福。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Director Wei Yingzhao to reinvestigate and the verdict was changed to convict Fu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Director Wei Yingzhao to reinvestigate; the verdict was reversed and Fu was convicted.

sentences.zh: 東廠奏法司妄出人罪，帝怒，下應召詔獄。

translations.literal: The Eastern Depot memorialized that the judicial offices had recklessly released a guilty man—the emperor was enraged and Wei Yingzhao was sent to the edict prison.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Depot reported that the courts had wrongly freed a guilty man; the emperor was enraged and sent Wei Yingzhao to the edict prison.

sentences.zh: 浹是應召議，執如初。

translations.literal: Jia sided with Yingzhao's finding and held to the original verdict.
translations.idiomatic: Jia sided with Yingzhao and upheld the revised verdict.

sentences.zh: 帝愈怒，褫浹職。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still angrier and stripped Jia of office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angrier still and stripped Jia of office.

sentences.zh: 給事中陸粲、劉希簡爭之，帝大怒，並下兩人詔獄。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Lu Can and Liu Xijian disputed this; the emperor was greatly enraged and both men were also sent to the edict prison.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Lu Can and Liu Xijian protested; the emperor was furious and sent both to the edict prison as well.

sentences.zh: 侍郎許贊等遂抵柱死，應召及鄰人俱充軍，杖福姊百，人以為冤。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Xu Zan and others thereupon upheld Zhu's death sentence; Yingzhao and the neighbors were all sentenced to military exile, Fu's elder sister was beaten a hundred blows—people considered it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Xu Zan and others then upheld Zhu's death sentence; Yingzhao and the neighbors were banished to military service, and Fu's sister was flogged a hundred times—many considered it a miscarriage of justice.

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝方深疾孝、武兩後家，柱實武宗後家夏氏仆，故帝必欲殺之。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor deeply resented the families of the Xia and Wu empresses; Zhu was in fact a servant of Empress Xia of Emperor Wuzong's family, and therefore the emperor was determined to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor deeply resented the consort families of the Xia and Wu empresses; Zhu was in fact a servant of Empress Xia's clan from the Wuzong era, and the emperor was determined to see him dead.

sentences.zh: 浹家居十年。

translations.literal: Jia lived at home for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Jia lived in retirement for ten years.

sentences.zh: 至帝幸承天與近臣論舊人，乃召為南京禮部尚書，改兵部，參贊機務。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Chengtian and discussed old associates with close ministers, Jia was recalled as Minister of Rites at Nanjing, then changed to the Ministry of War to assist in deliberating on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Chengtian and spoke with close ministers about old servants, Jia was recalled as Nanjing Minister of Rites, then shifted to the Ministry of War to assist in state deliberations.

sentences.zh: 二十一年召為兵部尚書，掌都察院事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was recalled as Minister of War and directed Court of Censors affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was recalled as Minister of War and put in charge of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 居二年，代許贊為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: After two years he replaced Xu Zan as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he replaced Xu Zan as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝於禁中築乩仙臺，間用其言決威福，浹論其妄。

translations.literal: The emperor had built a planchette spirit platform in the palace and occasionally used its pronouncements to decide authority and favor; Jia argued that this was deluded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had built a spirit-writing platform in the palace and sometimes let its pronouncements decide rewards and punishments; Jia argued this was deluded.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，欲罪之，以前議禮故不遽斥。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and wished to punish him, but because of his earlier service in the rites debate did not immediately dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and wanted to punish him, but because of his earlier role in the rites debate did not dismiss him at once.

sentences.zh: 二品六年滿，加太子太保，坐事奪俸者再。

translations.literal: When six years at the second rank were complete he was granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; twice he had salary forfeited on account of offenses.
translations.idiomatic: After six years at the second rank he was granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, though twice his salary was forfeited for offenses.

sentences.zh: 浹知帝意終不釋，遂稱病乞休。

translations.literal: Jia knew the emperor's mind would never release its grievance and therefore claimed illness and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Jia knew the emperor would never forgive him and claimed illness, asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，褫職為民。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and stripped him of office, reducing him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and stripped him of office, reducing him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 又十年卒。

translations.literal: After another ten years he died.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later he died.

sentences.zh: 浹少有誌節，自守嚴。

translations.literal: Jia from youth had resolve and integrity; he maintained strict self-restraint.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xiong Jia had resolve and integrity, and he held himself to strict standards.

sentences.zh: 雖由議禮顯，然不甚黨比，尤愛護人才。

translations.literal: Although he rose to prominence through the rites debate, yet he was not much given to factional alliance and was especially protective of talented men.
translations.idiomatic: Although he rose to prominence through the Rites Controversy, he was not much given to factional alliance and was especially protective of talented men.

sentences.zh: 故其去吏部也，善類多思之。

translations.literal: Therefore when he left the Ministry of Personnel, good men greatly missed him.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when he left the Ministry of Personnel, worthy men greatly missed him.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，復官，予祭葬，謚恭肅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing his office was restored; he was granted sacrificial honors at burial and posthumously titled Gongsu.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign his office was restored; he was granted state burial rites and posthumously titled Gongsu.

sentences.zh: 黃宗明，字誠甫，鄞人。

translations.literal: Huang Zongming, styled Chengfu, was a native of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zongming, styled Chengfu, was a native of Yin.

sentences.zh: 正德九年進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhengde he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the ninth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 除南京兵部主事，進員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed director in the Nanjing Ministry of War and promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a director in the Nanjing Ministry of War and later promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 嘗從王守仁論學。

translations.literal: He once studied learning under Wang Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: He once studied under Wang Shouren.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠反，上江防三策。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Ning, Chen Hao, rebelled, he submitted three strategies for river defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Ning, Chen Hao, rebelled, he submitted three strategies for Yangtze River defense.

sentences.zh: 武宗南征，抗疏諫，尋請告歸。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong marched south, he memorialized in opposition; soon he requested leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong marched south on campaign, he submitted a memorial in protest; soon afterward he asked for leave and returned home.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年，起南京刑部郎中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing he was recalled as director in the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jiajing reign he was recalled as a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 張璁、桂萼爭「大禮」，自南京召入都，未上。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong and Gui E contested the "Great Rites"; summoned from Nanjing to the capital, they had not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong and Gui E were contesting the "Great Rites"; they had been summoned from Nanjing to the capital but had not yet arrived.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，璁、萼、黃綰及宗明聯疏奏曰：「今日尊崇之議，以陛下與為人後者，禮官附和之私也。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, Cong, E, Huang Wan, and Zongming jointly memorialized, saying: "Today's debate over honoring the emperor—that Your Majesty was made another's heir is the private flattery of the rites officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year, Zhang Cong, Gui E, Huang Wan, and Huang Zongming submitted a joint memorial, saying: "Today's debate over imperial honors holds that Your Majesty was made another's heir—that is the private flattery of the rites officials.

sentences.zh: 以陛下為入繼大統者，臣等考經之論也。

translations.literal: That Your Majesty entered to succeed the great succession is our conclusion from examining the classics.
translations.idiomatic: That Your Majesty entered to succeed the great succession is our conclusion from examining the classics.

sentences.zh: 人之言曰，兩議相持，有大小眾寡不敵之勢。

translations.literal: People say the two positions stand opposed, with disparities of rank, number, and strength.
translations.idiomatic: People say the two positions stand opposed, with unequal rank, numbers, and strength on each side.

sentences.zh: 臣等則曰，惟理而已。

translations.literal: We say only principle matters.
translations.idiomatic: We say that only principle matters.

sentences.zh: 大哉舜之為君，視天下悅而歸己，猶草芥也，惟不順於父母，如窮人無所歸。

translations.literal: How great was Shun as ruler—he regarded the whole realm rejoicing and coming to him as grass, yet when he was not filial toward his parents he felt like a destitute man with nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: How great was Shun as ruler: he regarded the whole realm rejoicing and coming to him as no more than grass, yet when he was not filial toward his parents he felt like a destitute man with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 今言者徇私植黨，奪天子之父母而不顧，在陛下可一日安其位而不之圖乎？

translations.literal: Those who speak now favor private interest and cultivate factions, seizing the Son of Heaven's parents without regard—can Your Majesty rest secure in your throne for a day without considering this?
translations.idiomatic: Those who speak now favor private interest and cultivate factions, seizing the Son of Heaven's parents without regard—can Your Majesty rest secure on the throne for even a day without considering this?

sentences.zh: 此聖諭令廷臣集議，終日相視莫敢先發者，勢有所壓，理有所屈故也。

translations.literal: This is why the holy edict ordered court officials to deliberate together, yet for a whole day they looked at one another and none dared speak first—pressure from power bent principle.
translations.idiomatic: This is why, when the holy edict ordered court officials to deliberate together, they looked at one another all day and none dared speak first—power bent principle.

sentences.zh: 臣等大懼欺蔽因循，終不能贊成大孝。

translations.literal: We greatly fear deception, procrastination, and ultimately failing to help accomplish supreme filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: We greatly fear deception and procrastination, and that in the end we will fail to help accomplish supreme filial piety.

sentences.zh: 陛下何不親禦朝堂，進百官而詢之曰：『朕以憲宗皇帝之孫，孝宗皇帝之侄，興獻帝之子，遵太祖兄終弟及之文，奉武宗倫序當立之詔，入承大統，非與為人後者也。

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty not personally attend court, summon the hundred officials, and ask: 'I am the grandson of Emperor Xianzong, the nephew of Emperor Xiaozong, and the son of Emperor Xingxian; following the precedent of the Taizu that when the elder brother dies the younger succeeds, and obeying the decree that Wuzong's line in turn should hold the succession, I entered to inherit the great succession—I am not one who was made another's heir.
translations.idiomatic: Why does Your Majesty not personally attend court, summon the hundred officials, and ask: 'I am the grandson of Emperor Xianzong, the nephew of Emperor Xiaozong, and the son of Emperor Xingxian; following the Taizu's precedent that when the elder brother dies the younger succeeds, and obeying the decree that Wuzong's line in turn should hold the succession, I entered to inherit the great succession—I am not one who was made another's heir.

sentences.zh: 前者未及詳稽，遽詔天下，尊孝宗皇帝為皇考，昭聖太后為聖母，而興獻帝後別加本生之稱，朕深用悔艾。

translations.literal: Earlier, before matters could be fully examined, an edict was hastily issued throughout the realm honoring Emperor Xiaozong as Imperial Father and Empress Dowager Zhaosheng as Holy Mother, while Emperor Xingxian was separately given his birth-parent title—I deeply repent this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, before matters could be fully examined, an edict was hastily issued throughout the realm honoring Emperor Xiaozong as Imperial Father and Empress Dowager Zhaosheng as Holy Mother, while Emperor Xingxian was separately given his birth-parent title—I deeply repent this.

sentences.zh: 今當明父子大倫，繼統大義，改稱孝宗為皇伯考，昭聖為皇伯母，而去本生之稱，為皇考恭穆獻皇帝，聖母章聖皇太后，此萬世通禮。

translations.literal: Now the great relations between father and son and the great principle of succession must be clarified: Xiaozong shall be called Imperial Uncle-Father, Zhaosheng Imperial Aunt-Mother; the birth-parent title shall be removed; Emperor Xingxian shall be Imperial Father Gongmu, and the Holy Mother Zhangsheng Empress Dowager—this is eternal ritual for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Now the great relations between father and son and the great principle of succession must be clarified: Xiaozong shall be called Imperial Uncle-Father, Zhaosheng Imperial Aunt-Mother; the birth-parent title shall be removed; Emperor Xingxian shall be Imperial Father Gongmu, and the Holy Mother Zhangsheng Empress Dowager—this is the eternal ritual for all generations.

sentences.zh: 爾文武廷臣尚念父子之親，君臣之義，與朕共明大倫於天下。』

translations.literal: You civil and military court officials should remember the intimacy of father and son and the righteousness between ruler and subject, and with me make the great relations clear throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: You civil and military court officials should remember the intimacy of father and son and the righteousness between ruler and subject, and with me make the great relations clear throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 如此，在朝百工有不感泣而奉詔者乎，更以此告於天下萬姓，其有不感泣而奉詔者乎，此即《周禮》詢群臣詢萬民之意也。」

translations.literal: Thus would any officer in court fail to weep with emotion and obey such an edict? And if this were proclaimed to all the people under Heaven, would any fail to weep and obey? This is the intent of the Rites of Zhou in consulting the ministers and the people.
translations.idiomatic: Would any officer at court fail to weep with emotion and obey such an edict? And if this were proclaimed to all the people under Heaven, would any fail to weep and obey? This is the intent of the Rites of Zhou in consulting ministers and the people.

sentences.zh: 奏入，帝大悅，卒如其言。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; the emperor was greatly pleased and ultimately did as they said.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was greatly pleased and ultimately did as they proposed.

sentences.zh: 宗明亦遂蒙帝眷。

translations.literal: Zongming also thereupon received the emperor's special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zongming also came under the emperor's special favor.

sentences.zh: 明年出為吉安知府，遷福建鹽運使。

translations.literal: The next year he was sent out as prefect of Ji'an and transferred to salt transport commissioner in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was sent out as prefect of Ji'an, then transferred to salt transport commissioner in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 六年召修《明倫大典》，以母憂歸。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned to compile the Great Canon of Human Relations and returned home on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was summoned to compile the Great Canon of Human Relations but returned home to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，征拜光祿卿。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was summoned and appointed director of the Court of Imperial Entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was summoned and appointed director of the Court of Imperial Entertainment.

sentences.zh: 十一年擢兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 其冬，編修楊名以劾汪鋐下詔獄，詞連同官程文德，亦坐系。

translations.literal: That winter, compiler Yang Ming was sent to the edict prison for impeaching Wang Hong; the accusation implicated his colleague Cheng Wende, who was also imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, compiler Yang Ming was sent to the edict prison for impeaching Wang Hong; the accusation implicated his colleague Cheng Wende, who was also imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 詔書責主謀者益急。

translations.literal: The edict grew still more urgent in demanding the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: The edict grew still more urgent in demanding the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 宗明抗疏救，且曰：「連坐非善政。

translations.literal: Zongming memorialized in opposition to save them, saying: "Collective punishment is not good policy.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zongming submitted a memorial in protest to save them, saying: "Collective punishment is not good policy.

sentences.zh: 今以一人妄言，必究主使，廷臣孰不懼？

translations.literal: Now that one man's reckless words require finding the mastermind, which court official will not fear?
translations.idiomatic: Now that one man's reckless words require finding the mastermind, which court official will not fear?

sentences.zh: 況名搒掠已極，當嚴冬或困斃，將為仁明累。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Ming has been beaten to the limit—if in deep winter he should die in custody, it will burden Your Majesty's reputation for benevolence and clarity."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Yang Ming has been beaten to the limit—if in deep winter he should die in custody, it will burden Your Majesty's reputation for benevolence and clarity."

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，謂宗明即其主使，並下詔獄，謫福建右參政。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged, took Zongming to be the mastermind, sent him to the edict prison as well, and demoted him to right assistant administrator in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, took Huang Zongming to be the mastermind, sent him to the edict prison as well, and demoted him to right assistant administrator in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 帝終念宗明議禮功，明年召拜禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: The emperor continued to remember Zongming's service in the rites debate; the next year he recalled him as vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor continued to remember Huang Zongming's service in the Rites Controversy; the next year he recalled him as vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 遼東兵變，捶辱巡撫呂經。

translations.literal: Troops mutinied in Liaodong, beating and humiliating Grand Coordinator Lu Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Troops mutinied in Liaodong, beating and humiliating Grand Coordinator Lu Jing.

sentences.zh: 而帝務姑息，納鎮守中官王純等言，將逮經。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor favored leniency, accepted the words of defensive eunuch Wang Chun and others, and intended to arrest Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor favored leniency, accepted the words of the defensive eunuch Wang Chun and others, and intended to arrest Lu Jing.

sentences.zh: 宗明言：「前者遼陽之變，生於有激。

translations.literal: Zongming said: "The earlier mutiny at Liaoyang arose from provocation.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zongming said: "The earlier mutiny at Liaoyang arose from provocation.

sentences.zh: 今重賦苛徭悉已厘正，廣寧復變，又誰激之？

translations.literal: Now heavy levies and harsh corvée have all been corrected—who provoked the new revolt at Guangning?
translations.idiomatic: Now heavy levies and harsh corvée have all been corrected—who provoked the new revolt at Guangning?

sentences.zh: 法不宜復赦。

translations.literal: The law does not permit another amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The law does not permit another amnesty.

sentences.zh: 請令新撫臣韓邦奇勒兵壓境，揚聲討罪，取其首惡，用振國威，不得專事姑息。」

translations.literal: I ask that the new grand coordinator Han Bangqi lead troops to press the border, proclaim the pursuit of guilt, take the ringleaders, and shake the realm's majesty—not rely wholly on leniency."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the new grand coordinator Han Bangqi lead troops to press the border, proclaim the pursuit of guilt, take the ringleaders, and restore the realm's majesty—not rely wholly on leniency."

sentences.zh: 帝不從，經卒被逮。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen; Jing was ultimately arrested.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen; Lu Jing was ultimately arrested.

sentences.zh: 宗明尋轉左侍郎，卒於官。

translations.literal: Zongming was soon transferred to left vice minister and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zongming was soon transferred to left vice minister and died in office.

sentences.zh: 初，議禮諸臣恃帝恩眷，驅駕氣勢，恣行胸臆。

translations.literal: Initially the ministers who had debated the rites relied on imperial favor, drove affairs with overbearing force, and acted on private impulse.
translations.idiomatic: At first the ministers who had debated the rites relied on imperial favor, drove affairs with overbearing force, and acted on private impulse.

sentences.zh: 宗明雖由是驟顯，持論頗平，於諸人中獨無畏惡之者。

translations.literal: Although Zongming rose suddenly through this, his positions were fairly measured; among them all he alone aroused neither fear nor hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Although Huang Zongming rose suddenly through this, his positions were fairly measured; among them all he alone aroused neither fear nor hatred.

sentences.zh: 黃綰，字宗賢，黃巖人，侍郎孔昭孫也。

translations.literal: Huang Wan, styled Zongxian, was a native of Huangyan; he was the grandson of Vice Minister Kong Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan, styled Zongxian, was a native of Huangyan and the grandson of Vice Minister Kong Zhao.

sentences.zh: 承祖蔭官後府都事。

translations.literal: He inherited office and served as director in the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited office and served as a director in the rear palace.

sentences.zh: 嘗師謝鐸、王守仁。

translations.literal: He studied under Xie Duo and Wang Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Xie Duo and Wang Shouren.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，為南京都察院經歷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he served as registrar in the Nanjing Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jiajing reign he served as registrar in the Nanjing Censorate.

sentences.zh: 張璁、桂萼爭「大禮」，帝心向之。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong and Gui E contested the "Great Rites," and the emperor's heart favored them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong and Gui E contested the "Great Rites," and the emperor's heart favored them.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，綰亦上言曰：「武宗承孝宗之統十有六年，今復以陛下為孝宗之子，繼孝宗之統，則武宗不應有廟矣。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year Wan also memorialized, saying: "Wuzong held Xiaozong's succession for sixteen years—if now Your Majesty is called Xiaozong's son and inherits Xiaozong's line, then Wuzong should have no temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year Huang Wan also memorialized, saying: "Wuzong held Xiaozong's succession for sixteen years—if now Your Majesty is called Xiaozong's son and inherits Xiaozong's line, then Wuzong should have no temple.

sentences.zh: 是使孝宗不得子武宗，乃所以絕孝宗也。

translations.literal: This prevents Xiaozong from having Wuzong as son and thus cuts off Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: This prevents Xiaozong from having Wuzong as son and thus cuts off Xiaozong.

sentences.zh: 由是，使興獻帝不得子陛下，乃所以絕興獻帝也。

translations.literal: By this, it prevents Emperor Xingxian from having Your Majesty as son and thus cuts off Emperor Xingxian.
translations.idiomatic: By this, it prevents Emperor Xingxian from having Your Majesty as son and thus cuts off Emperor Xingxian.

sentences.zh: 不幾於三綱淪，九法棨哉！」

translations.literal: Does this not nearly overturn the three bonds and throw the nine laws into chaos!"
translations.idiomatic: Does this not nearly overturn the three bonds and throw the nine laws into chaos!"

sentences.zh: 奏入，帝大喜，下之所司。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; the emperor was greatly pleased and sent it to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was greatly pleased and sent it to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 其月，再上疏申前說。

translations.literal: That same month he memorialized again to develop his earlier argument.
translations.idiomatic: That same month he memorialized again to develop his earlier argument.

sentences.zh: 俄聞帝下詔稱本生皇考，復抗疏極辨。

translations.literal: Soon he heard the emperor had issued an edict calling his birth father Imperial Father; he again memorialized vigorously to argue against it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he heard the emperor had issued an edict calling his birth father Imperial Father; he again submitted a memorial vigorously arguing against it.

sentences.zh: 又與璁、萼及黃宗明合疏爭，「大禮」乃定。

translations.literal: He also jointly memorialized with Cong, E, and Huang Zongming over the issue, and the "Great Rites" were settled.
translations.idiomatic: He also jointly memorialized with Zhang Cong, Gui E, and Huang Zongming over the issue, and the "Great Rites" were settled.

sentences.zh: 綰自是大受帝知。

translations.literal: From then Wan enjoyed the emperor's special trust greatly.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Huang Wan enjoyed the emperor's special trust.

sentences.zh: 及明年，何淵請建世室，綰與宗明斥其謬。

translations.literal: The next year, when He Yuan petitioned to build an Eternal Shrine, Wan together with Zongming denounced the proposal as mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when He Yuan petitioned to build an Eternal Shrine, Huang Wan together with Huang Zongming denounced the proposal as mistaken.

sentences.zh: 尋遷南京刑部員外郎，再謝病歸。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to vice director in the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments and again sought leave on illness and returned home.
