translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to vice director in the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments and again asked leave on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 帝念其議禮功，六年六月召擢光祿少卿，預修《明倫大典》。

translations.literal: The emperor, remembering his service in the rites debate, in the sixth month of the sixth year summoned and promoted him to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainment to assist in compiling the Great Canon of Human Relations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, remembering his service in the Rites Controversy, in the sixth month of the sixth year summoned and promoted him to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainment to help compile the Great Canon of Human Relations.

sentences.zh: 王守仁中忌者，雖封伯，不給誥券歲祿；

translations.literal: Wang Shouren had fallen among the jealous—though enfeoffed as a marquis, he was not given patent and annual stipend;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouren had fallen among the jealous—though enfeoffed as a marquis, he was not given patent and annual stipend;

sentences.zh: 諸有功若知府邢珣、徐璉、陳槐，御史伍希儒、謝源，多以考察黜。

translations.literal: men with merit such as prefects Xing Xun, Xu Lian, and Chen Huai, and censors Wu Xiru and Xie Yuan, were largely dismissed through performance review.
translations.idiomatic: men with merit such as the prefects Xing Xun, Xu Lian, and Chen Huai, and the censors Wu Xiru and Xie Yuan, were largely dismissed through performance review.

sentences.zh: 綰訟之於朝，且請召守仁輔政。

translations.literal: Wan pleaded their case at court and also asked that Shouren be summoned to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan pleaded their case at court and also asked that Wang Shouren be summoned to assist in government.

sentences.zh: 守仁得給賜如制，珣等亦敘錄。

translations.literal: Shouren received grants as prescribed, and Xun and the others were also given recorded appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouren received grants as prescribed, and Xing Xun and the others were also given recorded appointments.

sentences.zh: 綰尋遷大理左少卿。

translations.literal: Wan was soon transferred to left assistant minister of the Court of Revision.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan was soon transferred to left assistant minister of the Court of Revision.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，璁、萼逐諸翰林於外，引己所善者補之，遂用綰為少詹事兼侍講學士，直經筵。

translations.literal: That October Cong and E drove the Hanlin academicians out and filled their posts with men they favored; Wan was then appointed junior tutor together with lecturing academician, attending the classics lectures.
translations.idiomatic: That October Zhang Cong and Gui E drove the Hanlin academicians out and filled their posts with men they favored; Huang Wan was then appointed junior tutor and lecturing academician, attending the classics lectures.

sentences.zh: 以任子官翰林，前此未有也。

translations.literal: Appointment to the Hanlin through an official's son had never happened before.
translations.idiomatic: Appointment to the Hanlin through the privilege of an official's son had never happened before.

sentences.zh: 明年，《大典》成，進詹事。

translations.literal: The next year, when the Canon was completed, he was promoted to tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the Canon was completed, he was promoted to tutor.

sentences.zh: 錦衣僉事聶能遷者，初附錢寧得官，用登極詔例還為百戶。

translations.literal: Nie Nengqian of the Embroidered Uniform Guard had first gained office by attaching to Qian Ning; under the accession edict's precedent he reverted to centurion.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Nengqian of the Embroidered Uniform Guard had first gained office by attaching to Qian Ning; under the accession edict's precedent he reverted to centurion.

sentences.zh: 後附璁、萼議「大禮」，且交關中貴崔文，得復故職。

translations.literal: Later he attached to Cong and E in the "Great Rites" debate and cultivated ties with the chief eunuch Cui Wen, recovering his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Later he attached to Zhang Cong and Gui E in the "Great Rites" debate and cultivated ties with the chief eunuch Cui Wen, recovering his former post.

sentences.zh: 《大典》成，諸人皆進秩，能遷獨不與，大恨。

translations.literal: When the Canon was completed all the others received promotions—Nengqian alone did not, and he resented this deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When the Canon was completed all the others received promotions—Nie Nengqian alone did not, and he resented this deeply.

sentences.zh: 囑罷閑主事翁洪草奏，誣王守仁賄席書得召用，詞連綰及璁。

translations.literal: He had the dismissed director Weng Hong draft a memorial falsely charging Wang Shouren with bribing the chief secretary to obtain recall, implicating Wan and Cong.
translations.idiomatic: He had the dismissed director Weng Hong draft a memorial falsely charging Wang Shouren with bribing the chief secretary to obtain recall, implicating Huang Wan and Zhang Cong.

sentences.zh: 綰疏辨，且乞引避。

translations.literal: Wan memorialized in his defense and also asked to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan memorialized in his defense and also asked to withdraw from office.

sentences.zh: 帝優旨留之，而下能遷法司，遣之戍，洪亦編原籍為民。

translations.literal: The emperor replied with gracious words keeping him, but sent Nengqian to the judicial offices and banished him to military service; Hong was also registered as commoner in his native place.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with gracious words keeping him, but sent Nie Nengqian to the judicial offices and banished him to military service; Weng Hong was also registered as a commoner in his native place.

sentences.zh: 綰與璁輩深相得。

translations.literal: Wan and Cong's circle were deeply united.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan and Zhang Cong's circle were deeply united.

sentences.zh: 璁欲用為吏部侍郎，且令典試南京，並為楊一清所抑，又以其南音不令與經筵。

translations.literal: Cong wished to appoint him vice minister of personnel and also have him preside over the Nanjing examinations—both were blocked by Yang Yiqing; moreover, because of his southern accent he was not allowed to join the classics lectures.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong wished to appoint him vice minister of personnel and also have him preside over the Nanjing examinations—both were blocked by Yang Yiqing; moreover, because of his southern accent he was not allowed to join the classics lectures.

sentences.zh: 綰大恚，上疏醜詆一清而不斥其名。

translations.literal: Wan was furious and memorialized with ugly slander of Yiqing without naming him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan was furious and memorialized with ugly slander of Yang Yiqing without naming him.

sentences.zh: 帝心知其為一清也，以浮詞責之。

translations.literal: The emperor knew in his heart it was Yiqing and reprimanded him with empty words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew in his heart it was Yang Yiqing and reprimanded him with empty words.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，出為南京禮部右侍郎，遍攝諸部印。

translations.literal: That October he was sent out as right vice minister of rites in Nanjing, with authority over all departmental seals.
translations.idiomatic: That October he was sent out as right vice minister of rites in Nanjing, with authority over all departmental seals.

sentences.zh: 十二年召拜禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was recalled as left vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was recalled as left vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 初，綰與璁深相結。

translations.literal: At first Wan and Cong were deeply allied.
translations.idiomatic: At first Huang Wan and Zhang Cong were deeply allied.

sentences.zh: 至是，夏言長禮部，帝方向用，綰乃潛附之，與璁左。

translations.literal: By now Xia Yan headed the Ministry of Rites and the emperor intended to employ him—Wan secretly attached to Yan and turned against Cong.
translations.idiomatic: By now Xia Yan headed the Ministry of Rites and the emperor intended to employ him—Huang Wan secretly attached to Xia Yan and turned against Zhang Cong.

sentences.zh: 其佐南禮部也，郎中鄒守益引疾，詔綰核實。

translations.literal: While assisting at the southern Ministry of Rites, Director Zou Shouyi claimed illness; an edict ordered Wan to verify it.
translations.idiomatic: While assisting at the southern Ministry of Rites, Director Zou Shouyi claimed illness; an edict ordered Huang Wan to verify it.

sentences.zh: 久不報，而守益竟去。

translations.literal: He took long to reply, and Shouyi ultimately left.
translations.idiomatic: He took long to reply, and Zou Shouyi ultimately left.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書汪鋐希璁指，疏發其事，詔奪守益官，令鋐覆核，鋐遂劾綰欺蔽。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Wang Hong, hoping to please Cong, memorialized exposing the matter; an edict stripped Shouyi of office and ordered Hong to reinvestigate—Hong then impeached Wan for deception.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Wang Hong, hoping to please Zhang Cong, memorialized exposing the matter; an edict stripped Zou Shouyi of office and ordered Wang Hong to reinvestigate—Hong then impeached Huang Wan for deception.

sentences.zh: 璁調旨削三秩，出之外。

translations.literal: Cong obtained an edict reducing Wan three ranks and sending him outside.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong obtained an edict reducing Huang Wan three ranks and sending him outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 會禮部請祈谷導引官，帝留綰供事。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Rites requested prayer officers for the grain-prayer ceremony, the emperor kept Wan to serve.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Rites requested prayer officers for the grain-prayer ceremony, the emperor kept Huang Wan to serve.

sentences.zh: 鋐於是再疏攻綰，且掇及他事，帝復命調外。

translations.literal: Hong then memorialized again attacking Wan and dredging up other matters; the emperor again ordered Wan transferred outside.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong then memorialized again attacking Huang Wan and dredging up other matters; the emperor again ordered him transferred outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 綰上疏自理，因詆鋐為璁鷹犬，乞賜罷黜以避禍。

translations.literal: Wan memorialized in his own defense, denouncing Hong as Cong's hawk and dog, and begging dismissal to avoid disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan memorialized in his own defense, denouncing Wang Hong as Zhang Cong's hawk and dog, and begging to be dismissed to avoid disaster.

sentences.zh: 帝終念綰議禮功，仍留任如故。

translations.literal: The emperor still remembered Wan's service in the rites debate and kept him in post as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still remembered Huang Wan's service in the Rites Controversy and kept him in post as before.

sentences.zh: 綰自是顯與璁貳矣。

translations.literal: From then Wan was openly at odds with Cong.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Huang Wan was openly at odds with Zhang Cong.

sentences.zh: 初，大同軍變，殺總兵官李瑾，據城拒守。

translations.literal: Initially the Datong garrison mutinied, killed the commander-in-chief Li Jin, seized the city, and held it.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the Datong garrison mutinied, killed the commander-in-chief Li Jin, seized the city, and held it.

sentences.zh: 總制侍郎劉源清、提督郤永議屠之。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Vice Minister Liu Yuanqing and Commissioner Qie Yong planned to massacre them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Vice Minister Liu Yuanqing and Commissioner Qie Yong planned to massacre them.

sentences.zh: 城中恟懼，外勾蒙古為助，塞上大震。

translations.literal: Inside the city panic spread; they secretly summoned Mongols for aid, and the frontier was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the city panic spread; they secretly summoned Mongols for aid, and the frontier was greatly shaken.

sentences.zh: 巡撫潘倣急請止兵，源清怒，馳疏力詆倣。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Pan Fang urgently asked that troops be stopped; Yuanqing was furious and rushed a memorial violently denouncing Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Pan Fang urgently asked that troops be halted; Liu Yuanqing was furious and rushed a memorial violently denouncing Pan Fang.

sentences.zh: 璁及廷議並右源清，綰獨言非策。

translations.literal: Cong and the court debate all sided with Yuanqing; Wan alone said it was not a good policy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong and the court debate all sided with Liu Yuanqing; Huang Wan alone said it was not a sound policy.

sentences.zh: 及源清罷，侍郎張瓚往代。

translations.literal: When Yuanqing was dismissed, Vice Minister Zhang Zan went to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yuanqing was dismissed, Vice Minister Zhang Zan was sent to replace him.

sentences.zh: 未至，而郎中詹榮等已定亂。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Director Zhan Rong and others had already quelled the disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhang Zan arrived, Director Zhan Rong and others had already put down the mutiny.

sentences.zh: 叛卒未盡獲，軍民瘡痍甚，代王請遣大臣綏緝之。

translations.literal: Rebel soldiers were not all captured; military and civilians were grievously wounded; the Prince of Dai requested that a senior minister be dispatched to pacify and restore order.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel soldiers had not all been captured, and soldiers and civilians alike were grievously afflicted. The Prince of Dai memorialized asking that a senior minister be sent to pacify the region and restore order.

sentences.zh: 疏下禮部，夏言以為宜許，而極詆前用兵之謬，語侵璁。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Rites; Xia Yan held that it should be granted, but violently denounced the error of the earlier use of troops, with words implicating Cong.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the Ministry of Rites. Xia Yan held that the request should be granted, but he also fiercely denounced the folly of the earlier military campaign, with remarks that implicated Zhang Cong.

sentences.zh: 璁怒，力持不欲遣。

translations.literal: Cong was angry and firmly opposed dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong was furious and firmly opposed sending anyone.

sentences.zh: 帝委曲諭解之，乃特以命綰，且令察軍情，勘功罪，得便宜行事。

translations.literal: The emperor tactfully reconciled them, then specially ordered Wan, and also instructed him to survey military morale, assess merits and faults, and act at discretion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tactfully mediated between them, then specially appointed Huang Wan to the task, instructing him to assess military morale, weigh merits and faults, and act at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 綰馳至大同，宗室軍民牒訴官軍暴掠者以百數，無告叛軍者。

translations.literal: Wan rushed to Datong; princely clansmen, soldiers, and civilians submitted petitions accusing official troops of violent plunder by the hundreds, with none accusing the rebel soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan hurried to Datong. Princes, soldiers, and civilians submitted petitions by the hundreds accusing the government troops of violent plunder, yet not one petition accused the rebel soldiers.

sentences.zh: 綰一無所問，以安其心。

translations.literal: Wan asked about none of it, to reassure their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan pursued none of these complaints, so as to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 有為叛軍使蒙古歸者，綰執戮之，反側者復相煽。

translations.literal: There was one who had the rebel soldiers summon the Mongols back; Wan arrested and executed him, and those wavering were stirred up again.
translations.idiomatic: When someone who had summoned the Mongols back on behalf of the rebels was found, Huang Wan had him arrested and executed, and those still wavering were stirred up once more.

sentences.zh: 綰大集軍民，曉以禍福。

translations.literal: Wan greatly assembled soldiers and civilians and explained fortune and disaster to them.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan gathered soldiers and civilians in a great assembly and explained to them the consequences of fortune and ruin.

sentences.zh: 罹害者陳牒，綰佯不問，而密以牒授給振官，按裏核實，一日捕首惡數十人。

translations.literal: Victims submitted petitions; Wan pretended not to inquire, but secretly gave the petitions to relief officials, verified them by investigating leads, and in one day captured dozens of ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: When victims submitted petitions, Huang Wan pretended to take no notice, but secretly handed the documents to relief officials, who traced each case and verified the facts. In a single day they seized several dozen ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 卒尚欽殺一家三人，懼不免，夜鳴金倡亂，無應者，遂就擒。

translations.literal: The soldier Shang Qin had killed three people in one household; fearing he could not escape, he beat the alarm gong at night to incite disorder; none responded, and he was then captured.
translations.idiomatic: The soldier Shang Qin had killed three members of one household. Fearing he could not escape punishment, he beat the alarm gong at night to incite another mutiny, but no one answered, and he was captured.

sentences.zh: 綰復圖形購首惡數人，軍民乃不復虞詿誤。

translations.literal: Wan again posted portraits offering rewards for several ringleaders, and soldiers and civilians no longer feared being ensnared by mistake.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan then posted portraits offering rewards for the capture of several chief offenders, and soldiers and civilians no longer feared being wrongly implicated.

sentences.zh: 遂令有司樹木柵，設保甲四隅，創社學，教軍民子弟，城中大安。

translations.literal: He then ordered officials to erect wooden palisades, establish mutual-responsibility groups at the four corners, create community schools, and teach the children of soldiers and civilians; great peace returned to the city.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered local officials to build wooden palisades, establish mutual-responsibility groups in all four quarters, found community schools, and instruct the children of soldiers and civilians. Great calm was restored within the city.

sentences.zh: 還朝，列上文武將吏功罪，極詆源清、永。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he submitted a list of the merits and faults of civil and military officers and fiercely denounced Yuanqing and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court, he submitted a detailed accounting of the merits and faults of civil and military officers, fiercely denouncing Liu Yuanqing and Qie Yong.

sentences.zh: 綰以勞增俸一等，璁及兵部庇源清，陰抑綰。

translations.literal: Wan received one grade of increased salary for his labors; Cong and the Ministry of War shielded Yuanqing and secretly suppressed Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan was granted one grade of increased salary for his service, but Zhang Cong and the Ministry of War shielded Liu Yuanqing and secretly worked against Huang Wan.

sentences.zh: 綰累疏論，帝亦意向之，源清、永卒被逮。

translations.literal: Wan repeatedly memorialized arguing his case; the emperor also inclined toward him, and Yuanqing and Yong were eventually arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan memorialized repeatedly on the matter, and the emperor also came to favor his view. Liu Yuanqing and Qie Yong were eventually arrested.

sentences.zh: 綰尋以母憂歸。

translations.literal: Wan soon returned home on account of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan soon returned home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 十八年，禮官以恭上皇天上帝大號及皇祖謚號，請遣官詔諭朝鮮。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, rites officials, on account of reverently proclaiming the great title of the Supreme Lord of Heaven and the posthumous title of the imperial ancestor, requested that officials be dispatched to proclaim this by edict to Korea.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, rites officials requested that envoys be dispatched to proclaim by edict to Korea the newly honored title of the Supreme Lord of Heaven and the posthumous title of the imperial ancestor.

sentences.zh: 時帝方議討安南，欲因以覘之，乃曰：「安南亦朝貢之國，不可以邇年叛服故，不使與聞。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was discussing an expedition against Annam and wished to use this mission to observe conditions there, and said: "Annam is also a tributary state; it cannot, because of its rebellion and submission in recent years, be kept from hearing of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then debating an expedition against Annam and wished to use the mission to probe conditions there. He said: "Annam is also a tributary state. We cannot, because of its recent rebellion and submission, keep it from hearing of this.

sentences.zh: 其擇大臣有學識者往。」

translations.literal: Select a senior minister of learning and ability to go.
translations.idiomatic: Choose a senior minister of learning and ability to go.

sentences.zh: 廷臣屢以名上，皆不用。

translations.literal: Court officials repeatedly submitted names, but none were used.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials repeatedly submitted names, but none were chosen.

sentences.zh: 特起綰禮部尚書兼翰林學士為正使，諭德張治副之。

translations.literal: Wan was specially recalled as Minister of Rites and Hanlin Academician to serve as chief envoy, with Tutor Zhang Zhi as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan was specially recalled as Minister of Rites and Hanlin Academician to serve as chief envoy, with Tutor Zhang Zhi as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 帝方幸承天，趣綰詣行在受命。

translations.literal: The emperor was then visiting Chengtian and urged Wan to go to the mobile court to receive his commission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then visiting Chengtian and urged Huang Wan to proceed to the mobile court to receive his commission.

sentences.zh: 綰憚往，至徐州先馳使奏疾不能前，致失期。

translations.literal: Wan feared going; upon reaching Xuzhou he first sent a messenger memorializing that illness prevented him from proceeding, causing him to miss the deadline.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan feared making the journey. When he reached Xuzhou he first sent a messenger ahead memorializing that illness prevented him from proceeding, and so missed the deadline.

sentences.zh: 帝責綰不馳赴行在，而舟詣京師為大不敬，令陳狀，已而釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Wan for not rushing to the mobile court but taking a boat to the capital as a great disrespect, ordered him to state the facts, and later released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Huang Wan for failing to hurry to the mobile court and instead taking a boat to the capital, calling this a grave disrespect. He ordered Huang Wan to submit a written account, but later released him.

sentences.zh: 綰數陳便宜，請得節制兩廣、雲、貴重臣，遣給事御史同事，吏、禮、兵三部擇郎官二人備任使。

translations.literal: Wan repeatedly proposed expedient measures, requesting authority over the senior ministers of Guangdong and Guangxi, Yunnan, and Guizhou, the dispatch of supervising secretaries and censors to serve with him, and that the ministries of Personnel, Rites, and War each select two directors as reserve envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan repeatedly proposed practical measures, requesting authority over the senior ministers of Guangdong and Guangxi, Yunnan, and Guizhou; the dispatch of supervising secretaries and censors to accompany the mission; and that the ministries of Personnel, Rites, and War each select two directors as reserve envoys.

sentences.zh: 帝悉從之。

translations.literal: The emperor fully agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted all of these requests.

sentences.zh: 最後為其父母請贈，且援建儲恩例請給誥命如其官。

translations.literal: Finally he requested posthumous honors for his parents and, citing the precedent of favors granted at the establishment of the heir apparent, asked that patents of appointment be issued to them matching his own rank.
translations.idiomatic: Finally he requested posthumous honors for his parents and, citing the precedent of favors granted at the establishment of the heir apparent, asked that patents of appointment be issued to them matching his own official rank.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，褫尚書新命，令以侍郎閑住，使事亦竟寢。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, stripped him of his new appointment as minister, ordered him to remain idle as vice minister, and the envoy mission was also abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged. He stripped Huang Wan of his new appointment as minister, ordered him to remain idle at the rank of vice minister, and the envoy mission was abandoned altogether.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒於家。

translations.literal: After a long while, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, he died at home.

sentences.zh: 綰起家任子，致位卿貳。

translations.literal: Wan rose from appointment as the son of an officeholder to reach the rank of vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan had begun as the appointed son of an official and rose to vice-ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 初附張璁，晚背璁附夏言，時皆以傾狡目之。

translations.literal: At first he attached himself to Zhang Cong; late in life he turned against Cong and attached himself to Xia Yan, and contemporaries all regarded him as scheming and cunning.
translations.idiomatic: At first he attached himself to Zhang Cong; later he turned against Cong and attached himself to Xia Yan. Contemporaries regarded him as treacherous and deceitful.

sentences.zh: 方「大禮」之興也，首繼璁上疏者為襄府棗陽王祐楒。

translations.literal: When the "Great Rites" controversy arose, the first after Cong to submit a memorial was Wang Yousi, Prince of Zaoyang in the Xiang princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Rites controversy arose, the first after Zhang Cong to submit a memorial was Wang Yousi, Prince of Zaoyang in the Xiang princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 其言曰：「孝廟止宜稱『皇伯考』，聖父宜稱『皇考興獻大王』。

translations.literal: His words were: "Emperor Xiaozong should only be called 'Imperial Uncle-Father'; the sacred father should be called 'Imperial Father, King Xingxian.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Emperor Xiaozong should only be styled 'Imperial Uncle-Father'; the sacred father should be styled 'Imperial Father, King Xingxian.

sentences.zh: 即興國之陵廟祀用天子禮樂，祝稱孝子皇帝某。

translations.literal: Even if the tomb and temple of the Xing princely state use the rites and music of the Son of Heaven, the prayer should call him Filial Son Emperor so-and-so.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the tomb and temple of the Xing princely establishment were served with the rites and music of the Son of Heaven, the prayer should address him as Filial Son Emperor [personal name].

sentences.zh: 聖母宜上徽號稱太妃，迎養宮中。

translations.literal: The sacred mother should receive an honorific title as Grand Consort and be welcomed into the palace to be supported.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred mother should receive an honorific title as Grand Consort and be welcomed into the palace to be cared for.

sentences.zh: 庶繼體之道不失，天性之親不泯。」

translations.literal: Thus the principle of succession would not be lost, and the kinship of nature would not be extinguished.'
translations.idiomatic: In this way the principle of legitimate succession would be preserved and the bonds of natural kinship would not be extinguished.'

sentences.zh: 時世宗登極歲之八月也。

translations.literal: It was the eighth month of the year in which Emperor Shizong ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the eighth month of the year in which Emperor Shizong ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 自時厥後，諸希寵幹進之徒，紛然而起。

translations.literal: From that time onward, those who sought favor and advancement rose in droves.
translations.idiomatic: From that time onward, men seeking imperial favor and advancement rose up in droves.

sentences.zh: 失職武夫、罷閑小吏亦皆攘臂努目，抗論廟謨。

translations.literal: Dismissed military men and idle petty clerks all rolled up their sleeves and glared, disputing the imperial deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed soldiers and idle petty clerks rolled up their sleeves and glared as they challenged imperial policy.

sentences.zh: 即璁、萼輩亦羞稱之，不與為伍。

translations.literal: Even Cong, E, and their cohort were ashamed to be associated with them and would not join their ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Even Zhang Cong, Gui E, and their circle were ashamed to be linked with such men and would not join their company.

sentences.zh: 故自璁等八人外，率無殊擢。

translations.literal: Therefore, apart from Cong's eight, generally none received special promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, apart from Zhang Cong's eight associates, few received any special promotion.

sentences.zh: 至致仕教諭王價，遂請加諸臣貶竄誅戮之刑，懲朋黨欺蔽之罪。

translations.literal: As for the retired instructor Wang Jia, he went so far as to request that demotion, banishment, and execution be added for all the officials, to punish the crime of factional deception.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia, a retired district instructor, went so far as to request demotion, banishment, and execution for all the opposing officials, so as to punish the crime of factional deception.

sentences.zh: 而最陋者南京刑部主事歸安陸澄。

translations.literal: And the most base of them was Lu Cheng of Gui'an, Principal Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The most contemptible of them was Lu Cheng of Gui'an, a principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 初極言追尊之非，逮服闋入都，《明倫大典》已定，璁、萼大用事，澄乃言初為人誤，質之臣師王守仁乃大悔恨。

translations.literal: At first he strongly argued against posthumous honors; when his mourning ended and he entered the capital, the "Grand Canon of Illuminating Human Relations" had already been fixed, and Cong and E were greatly in power. Cheng then said he had at first been misled by others, questioned his teacher Wang Shouren, and greatly regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: At first he had strongly argued against posthumous honors. When his mourning ended and he entered the capital, the Grand Canon of Illuminating Human Relations had already been settled, and Zhang Cong and Gui E were firmly in power. Lu Cheng then claimed he had originally been misled by others; when he questioned his teacher Wang Shouren, he was filled with remorse.

sentences.zh: 萼悅其言，請除禮部主事。

translations.literal: E was pleased with his words and requested his appointment as Principal Secretary in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E was pleased with his words and requested that he be appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 而帝見澄前疏惡之，謫高州通判以去。

translations.literal: But the emperor, seeing Cheng's earlier memorial, hated it and demoted him to Assistant Prefect of Gaozhou to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor, having seen Lu Cheng's earlier memorial, took offense and demoted him to assistant prefect of Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四年七月，席書將輯《大禮集議》，因言：「近題請刊布，多系建言於三年以前，若臣書及璁、萼、獻夫、韜，所正取者不過五人。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Jiajing, Xi Shu was about to compile the "Collected Discussions on the Great Rites" and said: "The recent request to publish mostly concerns memorials submitted before the third year. As for myself, Shu, and Cong, E, Xianfu, and Tao, those formally selected number no more than five.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year of the Jiajing reign, Xi Shu was preparing to compile the Collected Discussions on the Great Rites. He said: "The recent request to publish mostly concerns memorials submitted before the third year. As for myself, Zhang Cong, Gui E, Fang Xianfu, and Huo Tao, those formally selected number no more than five.

sentences.zh: 禮科右給事中熊浹、南京刑部郎中黃宗明、都察院經歷黃綰、通政司經歷金述、監生陳雲章、儒士張少璉及楚王、棗陽王二宗室外，所附取者不過六人。

translations.literal: Right Supervising Secretary Xiong Jia of the Rites Section, Director Huang Zongming of the Nanjing Ministry of Justice, Secretariat Clerk Huang Wan of the Censorate, Secretariat Clerk Jin Shu of the Communications Office, student Chen Yunzhang, scholar Zhang Shaolian, and the two princes of Chu and Zaoyang aside, those additionally selected number no more than six.
translations.idiomatic: Right Supervising Secretary Xiong Jia of the Rites Section, Director Huang Zongming of the Nanjing Ministry of Justice, Secretariat Clerk Huang Wan of the Censorate, Secretariat Clerk Jin Shu of the Communications Office, student Chen Yunzhang, scholar Zhang Shaolian, and the two princes of Chu and Zaoyang aside, those additionally selected number no more than six.

sentences.zh: 有同時建議，若監生何淵、主事王國光、同知馬時中、巡檢房濬，言或未純，義多未正，亦在不取。

translations.literal: There were contemporaneous proposals, such as those of student He Yuan, Principal Secretary Wang Guoguang, Vice Prefect Ma Shizhong, and Inspector Fang Jun, whose words were not pure or whose principles were largely not correct; these too were excluded.
translations.idiomatic: There were contemporaneous proposals by student He Yuan, Principal Secretary Wang Guoguang, Vice Prefect Ma Shizhong, and Inspector Fang Jun, whose language was impure or whose principles were largely unsound; these too were excluded.

sentences.zh: 其他罷職投閑之夫，建言於璁、萼等召用後者，皆望風希旨，有所覬覦，亦一切不錄。

translations.literal: As for other dismissed and idle men who memorialized after Cong, E, and others were summoned to office, all looked to the wind and sought to please, harboring ambitions; these too were entirely excluded.
translations.idiomatic: As for other dismissed and idle men who memorialized after Zhang Cong, Gui E, and the others were summoned to office, all looked to the prevailing wind and sought favor with ulterior ambitions; these too were entirely excluded.

sentences.zh: 其錦衣百戶聶能遷、昌平致仕教諭王價建言三年二三月，未經采入。

translations.literal: The memorials submitted in the second and third months of the third year by Nie Nengqian, a hundred-household commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and Wang Jia, retired instructor of Changping, had not been included.
translations.idiomatic: The memorials submitted in the second and third months of the third year by Nie Nengqian, a hundred-household commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and Wang Jia, retired instructor of Changping, had not yet been included.

sentences.zh: 今二臣奏乞附名，應如其請。」

translations.literal: Now the two officials memorialize asking that their names be appended; their request should be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Now these two men memorialize asking that their names be appended; their request should be granted.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 因詔「大禮」已定，自今有假言陳奏者，必罪不宥。

translations.literal: An edict was therefore issued: since the "Great Rites" had been settled, from now on anyone who falsely memorialized would be punished without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was therefore issued: since the Great Rites had been settled, from now on anyone who submitted false or opportunistic memorials would be punished without pardon.

sentences.zh: 至十二年正月，蒲州諸生秦鏜伏闕上書，言：「孝宗之統訖於武宗，則獻皇帝於孝宗實為兄終弟及。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year, the student Qin Tang of Puzhou submitted a petition at the palace gate, saying: "Emperor Xiaozong's line ended with Emperor Wuzong; thus the Emperor Xian was in fact elder-brother succession to Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year, the student Qin Tang of Puzhou submitted a petition at the palace gate, saying: "Emperor Xiaozong's line ended with Emperor Wuzong; thus the Emperor Xian was in fact a case of elder-brother succession to Xiaozong.

sentences.zh: 陛下承獻皇帝之統，當奉之於太廟，而張孚敬議禮，乃別創世廟以祀之，使不得預昭穆之次，是幽之也。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty inherited the line of the Emperor Xian and ought to enshrine him in the Grand Ancestral Temple, but Zhang Fujing's rites proposal instead created a separate dynastic temple to worship him, keeping him from the order of zhao and mu; this is to consign him to obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty inherited the line of the Emperor Xian and ought to enshrine him in the Grand Ancestral Temple, but Zhang Fujing's rites proposal instead created a separate dynastic temple for his worship, keeping him from the proper order of ancestral precedence. This is to consign him to obscurity.

sentences.zh: 又謂：「分祀、天、地、日、月於四鄰，失尊卑大小之序。

translations.literal: He also said: "Separating the worship of Heaven, Earth, Sun, and Moon at the four suburban altars loses the order of high and low, great and small.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Separating the worship of Heaven, Earth, the Sun, and the Moon at the four suburban altars violates the proper order of high and low, great and small.

sentences.zh: 去先師王號，撤其塑像，損其禮樂，增啟聖祠，皆非聖祖之意。

translations.literal: Removing the royal title of the Former Master, withdrawing his statue, reducing his rites and music, and adding a shrine to his father—none of these accord with the intent of the sacred ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Removing the royal title of the Former Master, withdrawing his statue, reducing his rites and music, and adding a shrine to his father—none of these accord with the intent of the sacred founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 請復其初。」

translations.literal: I request that the original arrangements be restored.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the original arrangements be restored.

sentences.zh: 帝得奏，大怒。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the memorial, he was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor received the petition, he was furious.

sentences.zh: 責以毀上不道，下詔獄嚴訊，令供主謀。

translations.literal: He charged him with slandering the sovereign and violating the Way, sent him to the imperial prison for rigorous interrogation, and ordered him to reveal the chief conspirator.
translations.idiomatic: He charged Qin Tang with slandering the sovereign and violating the Way, sent him to the imperial prison for rigorous interrogation, and ordered him to reveal the chief conspirator.

sentences.zh: 鏜服妄議希恩，實無主使者。

translations.literal: Tang admitted he had rashly debated in hope of favor and that in fact there was no chief instigator.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Tang admitted that he had rashly debated in hope of imperial favor and that in fact there was no chief instigator.

sentences.zh: 乃坐妖言律論死，繫獄。

translations.literal: He was therefore sentenced to death under the statute on demonic speech and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore sentenced to death under the statute on seditious speech and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 其後又從豐坊之請，入廟稱宗，以配上帝，則璁輩已死，不及見矣。

translations.literal: Later, following Feng Fang's request, the emperor entered the temple with the title Zong and was paired with the Supreme Lord; by then Cong's cohort was already dead and could not witness it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at Feng Fang's request, the emperor was enshrined in the ancestral temple with the title Imperial Ancestor and paired with the Supreme Lord—but by then Zhang Cong and his associates were already dead and could not witness it.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：席書等亦由議禮受知，而持論差平。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Xi Shu and the others also gained recognition through the rites debate, and their arguments were comparatively moderate.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Xi Shu and the others also won imperial favor through the rites debate, and their arguments were comparatively moderate.

sentences.zh: 然事以激成，末流多變。

translations.literal: Yet the affair was completed through agitation, and the later currents changed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the affair was driven to completion through agitation, and its later course changed greatly.

sentences.zh: 蓋至入廟稱宗，則亦非諸人倡議之初心矣。

translations.literal: For when the emperor entered the temple with the title Zong, that was no longer the original intent of those who had first proposed the controversy.
translations.idiomatic: For when the emperor was enshrined as Imperial Ancestor, that was no longer the original intent of those who had first proposed the controversy.

sentences.zh: 書、韜在官頗有所建樹，浹、宗明能自斂戢，時論為優。

translations.literal: Shu and Tao achieved considerable accomplishments in office; Jia and Zongming were able to restrain themselves, and contemporary opinion regarded them favorably.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shu and Huo Tao achieved considerable accomplishments in office; Xiong Jia and Huang Zongming knew how to restrain themselves, and contemporary opinion regarded them favorably.

sentences.zh: 至綰之傾狡，乃不足道矣。

translations.literal: As for Wan's scheming and cunning, it is not worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: As for Huang Wan's treachery and deceit, he is not worth discussing.
